Existence based Human Centric Contemplation

1

Prelude

It’s not definite when humans first appeared on Earth, but we have

no doubt about whether humans exist or not, as we ourselves are

living evidence of that. However, the question of what it truly means

to be human eludes us to this day. Throughout history, humans have

tirelessly endeavoured to explore and comprehend the depths of their

inner selves. Our quest to unravel our identity has spanned millennia,

yet we continue to thirst for understanding. Despite the vast array of

advancements in material science, the study of the human being

remains elusive. Countless research efforts have been devoted to this

pursuit, yet a comprehensive understanding of the human being has

remained beyond our grasp.

A. Nagraj is an individual like one of us; he embarked on a journey to

the solitude of Amarkantak in search of understanding human

nature. Amarkantak, renowned as a pilgrimage site in India, marks

the origin of the river Narmada. Shree Nagraj, who we now call Baba

ji, left his village Agrahar in Mysore province and came here in search

of answers to some questions. Undeterred by the challenges he

faced—dense forests, harsh weather, wild animals, scarcity of food,

and various discomforts—he persisted in his quest. Initiated by Shree

Chandrashekhar Bharti, the Shankaracharya of the famous Sringeri

Math, Shree Nagraj ji carried on with his austerities according to

traditional methods. Through unwavering dedication, he eventually

attained a state of samadhi. Yet, finding no answers to his inquiries in

2 this state, he pursued 'samyama'. Baba ji understood existence as

coexistence as a result of this pursuit. In coexistence, he understood

humans as a combined form of jeevan and body. The realisation of

the sentient and insentient nature being saturated in the omnipresent

power (Omnipotence), which we call by names such as God, Truth,

Brahma, etc., also happened. The entire orderliness in existence was

understood. He saw that all of nature is submerged, soaked, and

surrounded by Omnipotence (Paramatma).

From the year 1976 onwards, he started sharing his realisations with

those who came to him. During this period, notable scientists such as

Dr. C.V. Raman and Dr. Homi Bhabha, the president of the Atomic

Energy Commission, sought his audience. Simultaneously, ordinary

villagers, often deemed illiterate, also sought his guidance. He began

expounding the Truth, sharing profound insights with those who

listened. As people grasped the truths he articulated, some started

disseminating this wisdom through workshops titled "Jeevan Vidya".

We implored Baba ji to elucidate his understanding of existence and

jeevan so that an authentic document could be created for humanity.

In response, Baba ji presented Jeevan Vidya over a three-day period at

Anwari Ashram, near Charama, in the Bastar district of Madhya

Pradesh.

The presentation was recorded on video, and it was decided to

publish it in book form to ensure that this message reaches everyone.

With this intention, Baba ji's discourse on 'Jeevan Vidya' is presented

3 in this book. We are filled with immense joy today as we offer this

book to humanity. We hope and believe that this book will be

instrumental in dispelling delusions about the self and existence.

Rajan Sharma

Nandini Nagar, Durg

March 2nd, 1999

4

Translator’s Note

Dear Brothers and Sisters,

It is my great pleasure to offer you the English translation of “Jeevan

Vidya – Ek Parichaya”. It was originally narrated in Hindi by Baba ji

(Shree A Nagraj) about his life journey and realisation to a small

gathering at Anwari Ashram, Bastar Distt C.G. in 1997. This

introductory book gives a glimpse of Madhyasth Darshan

Co-existentialism, which he has propounded and positioned as the

alternative (vikalp) of idealism and materialism.

I started working on the English translation of Madhyasth Darshan

literature from 2007 on Baba ji’s suggestion. Translation will help in

your study, he had said. I also needed a way to make myself useful.

This book is an expression of my gratitude toward him. I have

translated this book in my capacity as a student of this Darshan.

Baba ji used to say, “Truth can be communicated in words to those

who want to understand.” Based on this premise, he presented his

realisation in Truth to the world in the form of literature. He wrote

Madhyasth Darshan in the Hindi language. If Truth can be

communicated in one language, then it should be possible to

communicate it in all languages. All languages, therefore, would

mean the same when they communicate the Truth. This is an effort

to make a bridge to Madhyasth Darshan for the English speaking

5 world. It is a Hindi-English combined edition, with original Hindi

text on the left as a reference and translated English text on the right.

This book has undergone a thorough peer review for more than a

year by Shree Puneet Chawla (Delhi), Shree Sanjeev Chopra (Delhi),

and Shree Surendra Pal (Raipur). I have respect and gratitude for

their understanding, commitment and consistent effort, which has

helped in improving this book’s accuracy and readability. All of us in

the review team feel that our understanding has improved from this

collaborative exercise. We feel this translation will still undergo

revisions in future, as we improve our understanding and learn from

the feedback we receive.

I want to also thank Shree B R Agrawal (Raipur) and Shree

Suryakant Agrawal (Raipur) for their support in the publication. It is

an honour to have this book published by Divya Path Sansthan,

which is responsible for publishing all Madhyasth Darshan literature

of Baba ji. I want to express my gratitude to Shree Sadhan

Bhattacharya (Manav Teerth, Kiritpur), who has provided

clarification from time to time for furthering my understanding. My

sincere gratitude to all Jeevan Vidya family who provided useful

suggestions, encouragement and support for this work. My sincere

gratitude to Baba ji’s family at Amarkantak who have been serving

tirelessly for furthering this Darshan. Lastly, I want to express

gratitude to my family, which has always been a pillar of strength and

support for me.

6 It is my hope that the tone, intent and content of the original book

gets conveyed through this effort. I take full responsibility for this

translation, and am committed to its improvement.

Rakesh Gupta

Bangalore

14 Jan 2023

Email: rakesh2715@gmail.com

Blog: http://madhyasth-darshan.blogspot.com

Jeevan Vidya: An Introduction

My fellow humans! I listened to the ancient Vedic scriptures of my

own volition, with no pressure from anyone. Upon understanding

these scriptures, a wish arose within me for how humans on this

Earth should be. This is the proclamation that emerged from within

me: "May the Earth be heaven, May humans be deities, May dharma

prevail, May goodness be eternal."

May the Earth be heaven,May humans be deities,

May dharmaprevail,May goodness be eternal.

I want to share the background of how this arose. This bodily

journey of mine began in a hard-working, selflessly serving, pious,

and reverential family in the Vedic tradition. As you are all aware,

every child that is born follows the faith of their parents, accepts the

constitution of one nation or another, receives the education

available in their tradition, and tries to follow the path set out by

their teachers. I too started going through all these at the place and

family where I was born. Furthermore, there were dictates and

sanctions of tradition like, “Sit with these people, don’t sit with

those.” “Do this, don’t do that.” From the beginning and

throughout my childhood, I was dissatisfied with such dogmas. At

first, my elders thought all this was due to my young age. However, as

time passed, their attitude towards me started changing. I felt my

elders were unhappy with me; the first cause of my questioning

8 became this. But how was I to make them happy! If I did as they said,

I couldn’t keep myself from testing them against their own standards.

I could see that my elders were not always happy while living with

those protocols. That was the crux point. I started feeling that while

my elders instructed me on what to do and what not to do, whether

they themselves did those things or not, they were not happy all the

time. Even though it was not possible to find more reverential or

bigger scholars of scriptures than them anywhere. As a result of this

situation, I concluded that I would never blindly follow the dictates

and sanctions of tradition. It started becoming like a sacred oath for

me. Another factor that got added to this was that my elders could

not make me understand. All in all, the more they failed, the more

my conceit grew. The growth in my conceit and my not adhering to

the stereotypes happened simultaneously. What could we have done

if we continued in this manner?

Now, my elders began claiming that I hadn’t understood the Vedas,

Vedanta, and scriptures. They worried, "He rejects everything in a

self-proclaimed manner; how far can this be right?" This became the

cause of my second question. Now, what could I do? With no other

way left, I chose to study Vedanta, which they believed to be the

supreme knowledge.

The first stage is Vedanta – which is the karma of Vedic ideology.

According to the Vedic ideology, karma is that which begets heaven,

and all the rest is called something else. Upasana refers to the rituals

9 and ceremonies for becoming deities, known as Vedic worship. In the

third aspect, it is said that knowledge alone is supreme. When I asked,

"What is knowledge?" The answer was “Knowledge of Brahma.”

"Then what is Brahma?" I inquired. They replied, "You won’t

understand." Without understanding, how will we overcome it?

They assured that adhering to the dictates and sanctions of the

scriptures is the way. My elders then assured me that one gets the

answers to all questions in the state of samadhi. Thus, I concluded

that I must see the state of samadhi for myself. There was no other

option left for me. There was no point in arguing anymore. Agreeing

or disagreeing with them now was of no consequence. I had to find

the answers to my questions. After thoroughly listening to Vedanta,

the first question that formed in me was: What is bandhan (bondage)

and what is moksha (liberation)? They say that we live in bandhan

due to maya. Moksha is the dissolution of atma into Brahma. Where

did atma come from? They say, "Brahma itself resides in the heart of

jeeva in the form of atma." If atma has to ultimately dissolve into

Brahma for the liberation of jeeva, ending the cycles of birth-death

and its trips to heaven and hell, then why did Brahma bother to go

and sit in the hearts of jeeva in the first place? When the first jeeva

came into existence, it had no atma in it, so what was the need for

Brahma to go and sit inside it? My questioning seemed like being the

devil’s advocate. As I didn’t echo my elders, they called me the devil’s

advocate. I said, "You may be right, but you should still answer my

questions." But I didn’t get the answer to these questions. After this,

10 I was told that the answers would also be found in the state of

samadhi. What else could be done? I gradually began to prepare my

mind for samadhi.

All of this began in 1944, and by 1946 I had become mentally

prepared to pursue samadhi. It was also the time when the

conditions for Indian Independence were becoming ripe. Then, as

many of us had anticipated, the power got transferred from the

British to the Indian people in 1947. There were some great

visionaries and thinkers involved in the independence movement, but

I also observed some detrimental changes that happened in them

along with this success. This, too, caused me pain. After that, one

more hope got kindled. It was the hope that we (the Indian Nation)

would now have our own constitution, and perhaps that

constitution would provision evaluation of an authentic human. I

kept thinking and hoping that the constitution would show the way.

I used to avidly follow newspaper reports regarding the formulation

of the constitution. By the year 1950, after having considered all the

discussions, I concluded that it was impossible to evaluate an

authentic human under this constitution. This conclusion was based

on the fact that it had no description of the authentic human

character, which could be called the national character. So, what

could be done now? I had already accepted that all my questions on

Vedanta would be answered in samadhi. I concluded that this

question would also get answered in that state. There was no need to

argue with elders and scholars over this matter anymore. I decided

11 that either I would get all my answers in samadhi, or I would

consider my life an offering for learning.

One more person became ready to accompany me in this endeavour -

my wife. We had heard of Amarkantak as a sacred place from where

the holy river Narmada originates. With this noble thought in mind,

we decided to make one last attempt there and made the journey to

Amarkantak. After arriving, I started my sadhana using the Agama

Tantra Upasana method. This method, as prescribed in the

scriptures, aims for attaining samadhi by visualising all the deities in

every part of one’s body. It involves using one’s imaginativeness to

visualise and then worship these deities. This process of envisioning

deities in different parts of one’s body is called “nyas”. The

underlying formula provided in the scriptures for this practice is

‘देवोभूत्वादेवान्यजेत्’, which means, "you become like gods to worship

gods." All of this was conveyed to me, and I prepared myself to follow

it with complete honesty. I did my best to adhere to it. Eventually,

one day, I became free from the imagined proximity of the deities.

The awareness of "I am" remained. There were no other thoughts.

I had no thought of achieving something, having something, or

doing something in that state. This was something new, a small event

perhaps, which occurred. This state remained for a few hours after

the event. When I became aware of my body and time, I realised that

I had no awareness of these three things during that period. I had no

thoughts at all in that state. I became convinced that this had

happened to me. After this, I started thinking that I had achieved the

12 state of samadhi. I began repeating this state of samadhi every day

for several hours, anticipating that my questions would be answered.

However, even after years of waiting, I did not get answers to my

questions. This was the second failure. I did not get answers from

understanding Vedanta, and I did not get answers after achieving

samadhi. Even the highest scholars in my family could not provide

any answers. Where could I go now? There was no point in blaming

anyone, and so I continued living through this deadlock.

I had heard all about samadhi, and one day I had become confident

that I had attained it as well, but how would I be able to tell others

that this indeed was the state of samadhi? How could I ascertain its

firmness and what should I consider as its evidence? There was

nothing to describe in the state of samadhi; how could I present its

evidence? This curiosity deepened, and to test whether I had attained

the state of samadhi, I performed a practice called samyama. This

advice was also given by our ancestors. It is mentioned in Patanjali’s

Yoga Sutra – “धारणाध्यानसमाधित्रयमेकत्रत्वात्तसंयमाः”– These three –

dharana, dhyana, and samadhi – when practised concerning one

object, is samyama. Anyone can verify this reference. I could not

agree with what was written about samyama. Hence, I devised my

own design and method of samyama and subsequently carried it out.

As a result of practising samyama, I started seeing every bit of

existence in front of me. Here, seeing means understanding.

I have sequentially and systematically observed all the processes that

have taken place in emergence from a single atom to the vast earth. I

13 have achieved a state where I can impart this understanding to you.

Along with this, I also saw the ‘jeevan atom’ in the sequence of

atoms. The ‘jeevan atom’ is the same in me, in you, in a newborn

person, and even when it is without a body. I realised that jeevan

exists both with and without a body. Why does it exist with a body? I

will explain that later when the context arises.

I saw that ‘jeevan’ wants to evidence itself in the human tradition

through the body. That is the only formula here. What does jeevan

want to evidence? The answer I found is that jeevan first wants to live

and then, along with living, wants to become happy. Along with

being happy, it also wants to evidence itself. These are the three

stages. The first stage of wanting to live is fulfilled in the animal order

itself. The next two stages of wanting happiness and evidencing can

be accomplished only in humans and nowhere else. I have seen this

very thoroughly. I found this immensely satisfying. After that, in the

same vein, I discovered the formula for living with happiness –

“living in orderliness with resolution”.

The insentient world, which we call material order and biological

order, exists in solid, liquid, and gaseous states. I realised that there is

a combination of a great many rasa and rasayan at the root of

numerous formations of biological cells. Whatever else humans are to

do, they will keep doing. I saw that the composition of the body is

only from the combination of these substances. Both animal and

human bodies are composed only of physicochemical substances.

The essential difference I saw between animal and human bodies is

14 that the brain becomes fully enriched only in the human body. Being

enriched means the human brain has the capability for jeevan to

evidence itself in a multi-faceted way. I have seen this precisely.

After seeing all of this, it occurred to me that animal-kind is in its

orderliness, which is explained and clearly defined. Similarly, I

realised that humans too are clearly defined and explained in the form

of “inherent orderliness”, and they could live happily by living in this

manner. Along with this, I also found the answers to what exactly is

moksha? What is bandhan? In this state, I found the answer to the

questions that led me to this endeavour. I found that jeevan drives a

human body in order to evidence itself. What is to be evidenced? As

mentioned earlier, it is to evidence happiness. What is needed to

evidence happiness? One needs to become wise. Humans shall

evidence orderliness and happiness with understanding, and they will

not be able to do it in any other way. While I was doing sadhana,

everybody used to say that I live with such great discipline, restraint,

and precision. Hordes of people used to come to see me, but I bear

witness that my mind had no restraint in the initial stages of

sadhana. Until I attained samadhi, I did not have any mental

restraint.

I had only one resolve that I am here to do sadhana, and I am not to

do anything silly. But it was not that the silly thoughts didn’t arise in

my mind at all. On this basis, I can claim that until one attains

the state of samadhi, there is no method in existence for not

having silly thoughts. Humans naturally don’t want absurdity or

15 such thoughts, and the one doing sadhana definitely does not want

them. I also did not want them, yet they kept coming. This difficulty

is faced by all who practise sadhana. As long as the practitioner can

tolerate this, they persist with sadhana, and when they cannot, they

don’t. That’s all I can say in its final analysis.

Now I found the answer to what is bandhan and what is moksha.

Bandhan is ignorance or delusion. What is ignorance? To live like

animals. How can we consider animal behaviour to be evidence for

humans? If we assume animal living to be the evidence and model

human living according to that, then that would be a delusion for

humans. Traditions compel us to live with ignorance. Its testimony is

sex-obsessed psychology, consumption-obsessed sociology, and

profit-obsessed economics in the present education. It is ironic that

in the midst of this, people bless their children to become good,

moral, cultured, joyous and gentle! What is the correlation here?

What is the correlation between what we teach our children and

what we bless them to become?

I found the answer to my second question about national character

as well. What did I find? Each unit in existence has inherent

orderliness and participates in the overall orderliness. I found the

path for humans to achieve this as well. I discovered the definition of

human being. Awakened human being’s work and behaviour is

the embodiment of “humaneness”. When we articulate this work

and behaviour, it is called sociology or constitution. I understood

that imparting the understanding of humane conduct is the essence

16 of sociology. In this way, I found answers to both my questions. The

constitution shall provide the code of conduct of humaneness. We

can recognise the national character in the form of the constitution.

Further, when we become liberated from delusion, we can live as

humans ought to live – this itself is moksha. We don’t need to turn

ice into stone or stone into water. We don’t need to give ritual

blessings to anyone or perform any miracles or demonstrate

supernatural feats. There are no miracles or supernatural feats in

existence. I have seen it precisely. Even today, there are millions of

people trapped in the vicious cycle of curse and grace.

There is only one answer to this, the moment we take a single step in

the direction of awakening, from that moment all the curse, remorse,

and sin gets shattered. No taint of these remains. This can be

illustrated by the analogy of how we learn mathematics. One could

do a math question wrong a thousand times but once one has learnt

to do it right, then it becomes right for one’s whole life. As long as

one keeps making mistakes, each mistake is different until one learns

the right method. If a math problem is given to a million children

and they all solve it correctly, they will all arrive at the same answer. If

they all get it wrong, we could get a million different wrong answers.

Any common person can easily do this survey. With this, I discovered

one more formula –We humans are united in the right and

divided in the wrong.

Existence has only two kinds of realities. First, there are things that

can be counted as units, which we call Nature. Second, there is a

17 reality that pervades everywhere, which anyone can understand in a

moment. Each unit of nature is soaked, surrounded and submerged

in this second reality. This can be called Omnipresence. There are

two kinds of entities (units) – insentient and sentient. Sentient

entities mean animal-kind and humankind, and insentient entities

mean material order and biological order. Insentient entities include

all the minerals, soils, metals and formations of biological cells. All of

these are soaked, submerged and surrounded in Omnipresence. I

have seen this precisely. There is no provision in existence to separate

units of nature from Omnipresence. Humans cannot create that for

which there is no provision in existence.

If humans accomplish anything contrary to the usefulness of what is

provisioned in existence, it results in nothing but devastation. For

instance, we used so many resources for war, but we could

accomplish nothing other than the destruction of Earth and humans

through this. Perhaps the scientific community is slowly recognising

this. If they had recognised it sooner, humans could have become

happy and prosperous. Perhaps it was bound to happen in this way –

like the river that crosses many banks before it meets the ocean. First,

humans had to go through mystical idealism – but the relief found

here proved insufficient. After that, they found themselves in the

clutches of materialism again. The relief that they found here also

proved inadequate in terms of happiness and prosperity. This is the

painful situation of today.

18 We didn’t find complete relief from either of these and so naturally

there is a need for a third step. In this way, the answer that I found to

the question of bandhan and moksha is - “Humans become

liberated from bondage upon becoming wise.” Now, how can

one become wise? In the course of examining what I had seen, I asked

- what delusion do I have? I explored within “myself”, I verified

within “myself” and I found that there is no cause of bondage within

me. So why not work so that this state arises in everyone! What

would it be like if this happens? Then the proclamation that I had

shared with you will come true. Earth will become heavenly,

humans will become deities, dharmawill prevail, and goodness

will be eternal. The tradition of eternal goodness will be

established. Thus, I began examining myself by asking: Will I be able

to convey this knowledge? Do people have a need for it or not? Thus

began what we now know as JeevanVidya.

The point when I became confident (about the JeevanVidya

program) was when I realised that “the code of humane conduct” can

be incorporated into the Constitution. A humane national character

will become evident as a result. I am definite about this. I am myself

proficient and living evidence of this knowledge. I have understood

‘existence’ and I can impart that understanding to you. I have

understood ‘jeevan’ and I can impart that understanding to

you. I have understood ‘humane conduct’ and I can impart that

understanding to you. One becomes wise upon understanding

these three truths. What happens upon becoming wise? One

19 becomes liberated from bondage. What is this bondage? Bondage is

in the form of delusion. Our ancestors spoke about liberation from

the cycle of birth and death. The cycle of birth and death has nothing

to do with liberation. Nothing arrives at birth nor does anything

depart with death. All that is, exists forever.

Jeevan continues to exist even after death as it does while driving a

body. A piece of charcoal continues to exist in other forms even after

burning it. The scholars of physics and chemistry would have

understood this, and if they haven't, they are bound to, as is everyone

else. This is how one arrives at the understanding of truth. At the

fundamental level, a ‘reality’ never gets annihilated. Therefore, if

Earth remains healthy, and humans can live in orderliness, this would

be the basis of universal and eternal wellbeing. This wish of mine for

universal goodness rests primarily on the principle of humane

conduct. Humane conduct is the main pillar on which this wish of

mine for universal goodness rests.

The big benefit from this understanding will be that humans shall

live on this Earth forever - without wounding it, without tearing its

guts apart, and without destroying it. The way of such living also

emerges from this very understanding. Earth needs to first heal itself.

Whatever untoward events that humans have caused in their history

until now, all those are results of their ignorance. Humans inflicted

wounds on Earth, tore its guts apart, caused it fever and deformed its

surface in many ways. As a result, rivers and streams got destroyed, air

and water became polluted, and we all know the immense suffering it

20 has caused to humans. If Earth suffers, then all of the flora, fauna,

and humans that reside upon it are bound to suffer as well. You can

very well imagine what kind of people would have envisaged health

and happiness by wounding the planet.

The silver lining in the cloud is that if we stop disturbing its natural

balance, then it is reassuring to know that the resources on Earth's

surface are abundant enough for all humans to live on it. Mistakes,

crimes, revolts, and rebellions are the outcomes of human ignorance,

not understanding, which is evident as the imbalance everywhere.

Humans, along with Earth, rivers, streams, hills, and forests, have all

become imbalanced. We humans committed all these crimes during

the scientific age, yet we haven't stopped boasting about science! We

think science will find a lasting solution to this situation, even though

the human race is on the verge of being wiped out from Earth. We

need to pay attention to this. Humans will have to become wise

whenever they decide to avert this problem. There is no other way.

Crimes cannot be controlled through lack of understanding,

constitutional means or otherwise; a crime is still a crime. All the

nations on this Earth have their respective Constitutions. Each of

these Constitutions has three main agendas and a common theme -

‘Power-Centric Rule’. Power-Centric Rule gets implemented in the

form of three activities - stopping one mistake by making another

mistake, stopping one crime by committing another crime, and

stopping one war by waging another war. Yet there is no evidence

anywhere if these three actions could rid us of crimes. Rather with

21 every passing day, month, year, century, these three have only been

increasing. History is full of accounts of wars becoming fiercer,

crimes getting more prevalent, and one mistake leading to another.

The pages of history give testimony of this.

If we search for the root cause, we find that humans alone are

responsible for creating these circumstances. Another significant

factor is the 'religious constitution'. All religions believe that humans

are fundamentally sinners, ignorant, and selfish. However, the reality

is different from this. To deliver sinners, turn the ignorant into wise,

and the selfish into charitable, each religion prescribes its methods,

ideals, duties, responsibilities, and rituals. This is very much

apparent. What has been the net outcome of these efforts? So far,

there is no evidence of any ignorant person becoming wise, any selfish

person becoming charitable, or any sinner being emancipated as a

result of these efforts.

I had mentioned earlier that sadhana is performed until samadhi is

achieved. During this period, there is no resolution in thoughts, and

the mind remains perturbed since it is suffering from problems that

drive one towards samadhi in the first place. The greatness of a

human being is seen only in terms of their sincere efforts until

samadhi. During sadhana, one may get all kinds of silly thoughts,

which get extinguished after samadhi. The alternative path is -

perform study, attain mastery, then evidence it in living.

22 It has also been observed that after attaining the state of samadhi, a

human being has no desire to do anything, achieve anything, or keep

anything. So, how did I develop the desire to present all this? I have

already mentioned to you that my pursuit of samadhi was not for

liberation or heaven; it was to find answers to my questions. When I

did not find answers in the state of samadhi, I began scrutinising

whether I had truly attained samadhi or not. During this scrutiny, I

understood all these concepts. This understanding emerged due to

the good deeds of humans, for their future, and for universal

well-being. It has not come out of books. This is a fact. My elders had

guided me only to the extent that I would find the answer in the state

of samadhi. To validate whether I had attained samadhi, I performed

samyama, and on that basis, these insights emerged. Human

understanding has evolved in a successive manner. History

documents how humans lived in the jungle age, the stone age, and

the iron age. Many people found relief with the advent of the age of

kingdoms. The promise was that the king would ensure the security

of life and property, but that hasn’t happened until now. Life and

property remain insecure; peace and harmony are further still. It is

natural for every family and sect to be concerned about the security

of their life & property and for peace & harmony.

Similarly, idealism emerged, but whatever relief people found in it

proved insufficient over time. When this became inadequate, it was

natural to reconsider, leading to the advent of science as a way of

thinking. Previously, there was no room for logic in the sermonising

23 of idealism. Idealism imposed dos and don’ts, labelling non-believers

as sinners and subjecting them to harassment, as documented in

history. Science was embraced because of its logical nature and its

invitation to reason. Moreover, the imagined heaven and the desire

for happiness began to materialise as people started to benefit from

various amenities provided by science. People enjoyed these benefits

extensively, but eventually, scientific achievements also proved

insufficient. Once again, humans began to feel restricted. Thus, they

oscillate between devotion-detachment and comfort-accumulation.

They pursue devotion-detachment when tired of

comfort-accumulation, and when disillusioned from

devotion-detachment, they revert to comfort-accumulation. Both

these pursuits may feel good in themselves, but there is a distinction

between “feeling good” and “being good”. Just because something

feels good doesn’t mean that it is good. For instance, drinking cold

water may feel good, but it is not a law that cold water is always good.

Someone could fall ill from drinking cold water, or develop a cough

from it. Therefore, both cold water’s feeling good or its not feeling

good cannot be universal. This pertains to conduciveness for the

body.

Due to the ideology of science, we are drifting towards instability and

uncertainty. Scientists have unsuccessfully attempted to describe

humans as machines. The scientists who describe humans as

machines themselves remain dissatisfied with that description.

Nowadays, understanding the mechanical functioning of humans is

24 a major topic of scientific research. Scientists believe that this

understanding will accelerate human behaviour, work, and thinking.

However, humans do not fit into this framework. Science assumes

the accuracy of the mechanistic view, which humans can

comprehend and deal with. Idealists, on the other hand, have

advocated the suppression of sensitivity, believing that humans

cannot understand or withstand sensitivity. Thus, the gap between

the two ideologies remains unchanged. Consequently, humans have

become ensnared in problems one after another, reaching the end of

life with these problems only. All in all, this is the way we have

reached our present condition.

The proposal I am presenting before humanity, I believe, is the result

of the virtuous acts of the entire human race. If I were to assess my

own effort for this, it is not worthy of such a significant result (which

I have achieved). It is akin to a one-tonne fruit growing on a tree; the

tree itself would break apart if that were to happen. A similar event

has occurred with me. This discovery is greater than my individual

effort. The main point is - who is the bearer of this effort? I have

precisely observed that the entity that bears results in excess of effort

in humans. Jeevan is the bearer. Jeevan is capable of carrying such

results. How? I have seen jeevan in the form of inexhaustible strength

and power. I can teach you to see this as well. If you have the quest,

you can also understand it and then impart that understanding to

others. I am confident that you need to understand this, so you will

eventually come around to it. It is clear that whatever jeevan does

25 through the body, the result of it always turns out to be more than

the needs of the body. It is a natural process. I have seen jeevan, and I

have seen humans as a combined form of jeevan and body.

So far, humans were unable to elucidate consciousness and existence

by the method of study. Wherever science has attempted to enlighten

people about existence, it has consistently revealed instability and

uncertainty, fostering notions of struggle and obsessions with profit,

consumption, and sex. We humans kept accepting these ideas, but

even after living accordingly, they did not become the basis of our

satisfaction. The testimony to this is that the point of satisfaction of

comfort and accumulation could not be determined. Hence, we have

been living with an internal conflict with these ideas. Now, it is

imperative to comprehend the proposition being presented here. Just

as I validate it through my own living, you too must undertake this

validation. Upon finding satisfaction in living accordingly, you will

naturally feel compelled to impart this understanding to others. The

proof of our comprehension lies in our ability to convey it to others;

this is the litmus test of our wisdom. My realisation is from having

seen coexistence. Humans can experience prosperity in coexistence by

producing more than the needs of their families. This understanding

shall manifest itself only as resolution in every aspect of behaviour. I

have witnessed the interconnectedness of these three, and how our

consciousness expands in the course of teaching and evidencing

these, even though the physical expanse of the body remains limited.

This proposal has ideas that extend far beyond the physical expanse

26 of a human being. Every human has that ability and longing for

kindling enthusiasm for this understanding in them. That’s the

essence and purpose of this proposal.

Science is a step in itself; its preceding step was idealism, which in

turn followed the step of the village and tribal world. Further back,

humans wandered in the jungles during the Stone Age. We have

progressed step by step to reach where we are today. We should

acknowledge the contribution of each step and be grateful for them.

Here, I have provided a general sequence of events that serve as the

backdrop to this discovery. In summary, I did not find satisfaction in

the finest offerings from tradition. I accepted that I am a responsible

person, and thus it is my responsibility to find answers to my

questions. Consequently, I endeavoured for this and not for anything

else. Through this intellectual effort, I realised that all humans can be

happy, dharma can prevail, Earth can become heavenly, and humans

can become deities. This motivation led me to present this discovery

to humanity, which is what I am currently doing.

Upon completely understanding existence, jeevanand humane

conduct, I achieved a state which I will now describe to you. I

attained confidence within myself after understanding. I didn’t

have to exert any effort for it. I started verifying this confidence in all

aspects of my living as well. In the same way, the respect for

excellence also became feasible. I could evaluate excellence, which

naturally results in having respect for it. We cannot respect what we

do not evaluate. Thirdly, I comfortably integrated this understanding

27 into my personality. I didn’t face any difficulty like I will not be able

to live based on this understanding by way of harmony in jeevan and

existence. I called this balance between talent and personality. I

could meet this criterion truly and fully. Fourthly, I became social in

behaviour. I started getting satisfaction within myself from

becoming social. As a benefit, I was left with no complaints with the

world. Now every moment I keep scrutinizing the meaningfulness of

my actions. I live meaningfully by fulfilling duties and responsibilities

in all my relationships. Fifthly, I attained prosperity. Though I was

born in a hardworking family and I knew how to do physical labour

and seva, but I didn’t then really understand the meaning of

prosperity. The meaning of prosperity was understood now. We

produce more than the needs of our family to experience prosperity.

In this manner, I acquired many wonderful qualities, which

collectively I have called “autonomy”. I attained autonomy within

myself; therefore, which you can also attain.

Once we attain autonomy, we can express, teach and offer this

understanding to the world. As a result, I began articulating it in the

form of literature. I titled this literature Madhyasth Darshan

Sah-Astitva-Vad (Co-existentialism).

Madhyasth Darshan has been presented in four parts. The first part

has been named – The Holistic view of Human Behaviour

(Manav Vyavhar Darshan). The name of the second part is – The

Holistic view of Human Action (Manav Karma Darshan). The

name of the third part is – The Holistic view of Human Practice

28 (Manav Abhyas Darshan). The name of the fourth part is – The

Holistic view of Human Realisation (Manav Anubhav

Darshan).

In this manner, I wrote the entire Madhyasth Darshan in four parts.

There are generative, degenerative and mediative powers or motions

in existence, which have their respective outcomes. Among these,

establishing the magnificence of mediative strength and power is the

wonderful goal of humankind. I too was very amazed upon seeing

this. Anyone who has gotten its sense - whether scientist, scholar or

commoner - becomes amazed.

The scientists are in the position of accepting the generative and

degenerative powers in nature, but so far, they have not been able to

understand the mediative strength and power in the form of purpose.

I think this has been a huge oversight and error. Therefore, now the

need has come to rethink, whereby we have worked here to

understand and expound the mediative force, the mediative power,

the mediative omnipotence, and the mediative jeevan, and called it

“Madhyasth Darshan”.

I have explained the co-existentialism ideology under three headings.

The first is Resolution centred Materialism (samadhanatmak

bhautikvad). Its focal point is: - The entire physical and chemical

world is manifested as inherent orderliness and participates in

overall orderliness. The insentient nature is participative

within itself and is also complementary to the sentient nature.

29 I have tried to describe it here. The erstwhile ideologies are

struggle-centred or conflict-centred materialism. While in the state

and motion of coexistence, there is no fight, no revolt, and no

snatching or robbing - instead, there is mutual

complementariness, celebration, joyousness, and continuous

progression. This is what I have tried to explain here. Literature is

literally just words! According to me, literature is an attempt, but a

human will understand only from another human. Most

importantly, here logic has science aligned with wisdom and

wisdom aligned with science. Wisdom means recognition of the

purpose.

We will analyse something if its purpose is understood and has been

recognised. You also know what happens if we keep analysing

without understanding the purpose. You can evaluate yourself

whether science has taken humankind to great heights or into a

vicious trap. Resolution centred Materialism posits that all physical

and chemical matter in existence is inspiration for humans to live in

orderliness. All units of nature are complementary to one another,

mutually helpful for their grandeur, and interrelated for further

progression. This is the way resolution is described here.

The name given to the second monograph of co-existentialism is –

Behaviour Centred Public Discourse (vyavharatmak janvad).

The path to satisfaction is through behaviour only. Behaviour is what

one human does with another. Human behaviour becomes defined

30 only in the form of humane conduct, and that’s what I have tried to

explain here.

After this, I wrote the third monograph, Realisation centred

Spiritualism (anubhavatmak adhyatmvad). So far, the world has

remained unsuccessful in explaining their belief in spirituality. We

can understand spirituality easily in just a few moments. It is the

emptiness between you and I, which is also visually apparent; we

could call it Space or Void or anything else. It’s there between you

and me, just as it is between this Earth and other planets. It’s also

there between one solar system and another, just as it is between one

galaxy and another. Space is uniform in all dimensions. Therefore, we

come to know that this reality is omnipresent. All entities (units) are

submerged, surrounded, and soaked in this omnipresent reality. This

itself comes into human realisation first. After that, one realises their

own being. Had this space not been between you and me, it wouldn’t

have been possible for me to realise your existence. Therefore, the

very first realisation happens in Omnipresence only. I have tried to

explain it here and highlighted the need for its understanding. How

will humans understand themselves without understanding

existence, of which they are a part? Therefore, understanding

existence is essential. All units of nature are in Omnipresence; this

itself is the testimony of coexistence. If we overlook the fact that

existence is coexistence, it results in nothing apart from problems and

suffering. Whatever revolts, rebellions, exploitations, and wars that

humans have committed until now, these all were contrary to the

31 principles of coexistence. It is ironic that even after doing all these, we

desired and hoped to achieve what is right.

Our hope remained unfulfilled, and we kept facing the consequences

of our actions. We laughed and cried amidst this. When one family or

community kills someone from the enemy side, they become very

happy, thinking they have eliminated their enemy. Governments and

nations think in the same way. The seats of religion are also based on

this thinking. Now, what should be done? Where can humans take

refuge now? In this way, delusion is found everywhere with no

direction or purpose, whether it is the seat of religion, the seat of

state, the seat of education, or the seat of business. Where should we

go? What should we do? These were the difficulties. I too had these

difficulties before awakening. Upon awakening, I became fully

determined that this whole discovery should reach the entire human

race.

After this, I wrote the treatises to describe how this understanding

shall manifest itself as the way of life. The erstwhile economic

theories are all obsessed with profit. It is very clear that human

happiness is not possible through such ideas. The only way to

happiness for all humans is through Cyclical Economics

(avartansheel arthshastra), which is practical and aligned with the

orderliness of nature.

I wrote the second treatise under the title Behavioural Sociology

(vyavharvadi samajshastra). Humans find satisfaction only when

32 there is justice in their behaviour with other humans. Humane

conduct is the focus here, which can be adopted as a model code of

conduct for the nation. Citizens of all nations can accept it as their

Constitution. This will lead to the indivisible society and universal

system, eliminating the constant fear of war between factions in the

world. As long as there are wars, humans will not be able to live

without disturbing the balance of Earth, and they will use even more

intellect to cause even bigger disturbances. We get an assessment of

the scientific intellect when we see that a great deal of science and a

great many scientists are currently devoted to the war effort, for

which they get money and feel accomplished, even though all this

leads to nothing but the destruction of the Earth. We will have to be

liberated from this, and for that there is no other way apart from our

becoming wise.

The third treatise that I wrote is – Psychology of Humane

Consciousness (manav sanchetnavadi manovigyan). It postulates

that jeevanis at the root of humane consciousness. The body is its

medium for expressing humane consciousness in the sense of

completeness in the human tradition. I have tried to explain this here.

Now, it is for you to examine.

My writing will be worthwhile if you understand it. In this way, I

have offered these three - the holistic view (darshan), the ideology

(vaad), and the treatises (shastra). The basic intent of treatises is to

describe that humans are to live in orderliness. How should humans

live? What is the way? What is the policy? What is the procedure?

33 These have been explained in the treatises. After this came the plans

for their implementation in three forms.

The first plan is the "Jeevan Vidya Plan" (jeevan vidya yojana).

Humans have remained ignorant about the self since ancient times.

Even in the age of idealism, attempts were made to explain concepts

like atma and paramatma through sermons, but they were

unsuccessful. This ignorance about the self has been a major source

of distress for humans. If the self is understood, then everything that

follows will also be understood. The Jeevan Vidya plan is designed to

overcome this very hurdle. The central point of this plan is to impart

the understanding of jeevan. There is equal potential in all humans,

young or old, to comprehend it. Jeevan is the basis of equality among

humans. The bodies of any two humans are never the same, but

jeevan exists in the same form in all humans. The strengths and

powers of jeevan are the same, and the goal of every jeevan is the

same.

Jeevan wants to become awakened, and awakening is its goal. Every

human seeks resolution and justice. All of us can verify this fact.

There is no part of the body that is awaiting or desiring justice, nor is

there any part that seeks resolution. Similarly, no part of the body

desires prosperity, even though every human naturally yearns for

justice, resolution, and prosperity. Therefore, the conclusion is that

justice, resolution, prosperity, and truth are the desires of jeevan

because humans are a combination of jeevan and body. It is

imperative to understand jeevan and its activities, and to comprehend

34 justice, dharma, and truth for jeevan’s satisfaction. This, in a nutshell,

is the task ahead. The Jeevan Vidya Plan has been presented based on

this understanding, which turned into a program. The stalwarts of

science and those who don’t know any science, the learned ones, and

the ordinary people - have all heard this proposal. Some have

understood it and are making efforts for others to understand it, and

have become successful. It was then that I became confident that

what I have understood is relevant and authentic, that everyone can

understand it, and upon understanding they can make others

understand.

The second plan is Humanisation of Education (shiksha ka

manviyakaran). To become wise is everyone’s inherent need.

Therefore, let us incorporate the entire content of the understanding

into education. We made a curriculum to that end and experimented

with it in a school. This school was at Govindpur in Bijnaur district,

and it was a very good experience there. There is a long-standing

belief of educationists that the environment affects the students, but

in Govindpur, we experienced that the students affect their

environment. We aspire to see this success on a large scale, and are

making efforts towards this.

The third plan is Family based Self-Governing System (parivar

moolak svarajya vyavastha). It is to bring about a resolution centric

system in place of the power-centric rule.

35 This understanding has thus been articulated in the form of the

holistic view, the ideology, the treatises and the plans.

May there be universal well-being!

36

Jeevan Vidya

I have understood jeevan, and from here begins the effort to impart

this understanding to you. This process is called "Jeevan Vidya." I

want to first clarify that jeevan is eternally the same. Everyone wants

to know and believe the reality of jeevan, and to evidence this

understanding. This is the basic objective. Jeevan is neither physical

nor non-physical. It is a constitutionally complete atom and a

sentient entity. What is constitutional completeness? This atom’s

constitution doesn’t undergo the expulsion or insertion of particles.

However, insertion and expulsion are found in the atoms in

physicochemical forms, which are called 'results' - whereby the

number of constituent particles in such atoms gets altered. This is the

only elemental transformation possible in the world. Whenever

humans are able to bring about any elemental transformation

in nature, it will be limited to altering the number of particles

in the evolving-constitution atoms. Such atoms are of two kinds –

hungry atoms and overfull atoms. The atoms that remain in hunger

(need) of some particles to become satiated, even as each result is a

state of being that exhibits wholeness, have been called "hungry

atoms." The atoms wherein some particles want to exit have been

called "overfull atoms." In this way, the activity of both kinds of

atoms is only towards satiety.

The satiated atom is a constitutionally complete atom. This itself is

the sentient unit (or jeevan). It has been called the sentient unit

37 because it harbours the capacity to manifest conscience and

sensitivity within the human tradition. Without jeevan, even if

humans were to succeed in artificially constructing the body,

they would be unable to evidence sensitivity, let alone

conscience. Therefore, humans can live in harmony and contribute

to the universal orderliness of existence only in the course of

evidencing their sensitivity and conscience. That is all the work there

is! All living beings of animal order evidence sensitivity. Humans,

however, don’t become satisfied or happy without evidencing

conscience, regardless of how hard they may try.

Humans inherently seek happiness. In our pursuit of happiness, we

sometimes believe that we will find it through comfort and

accumulation, and at other times through prayer and penance, or

devotion and detachment. All humans make efforts to achieve

happiness, yet there is no evidence that these efforts have led anyone

to lasting satisfaction and continuous happiness. In my own pursuit

of happiness, I have found it through understanding; similarly, I

believe that every person can achieve happiness through

understanding. In truth, all humans are united in the right and

divided in the wrong. Therefore, it was necessary to identify the

entity that is equally present in every human and can be the bearer

and carrier of understanding. I realised that entity is ‘jeevan’ living

with resolution.

When ‘jeevan’ lives with understanding, it presents resolution

everywhere. Every person is happy with resolution and unhappy with

38 problems. The entity that understands is jeevan, which drives the

human body. Whatever we have taught animals is within the realm of

sensitivity. But how does one human make another understand? No

one has ever been able to force understanding upon another. A

person may remain restrained by the fear of livelihood for some time,

but eventually, they shed that fear. The end of slavery in history

exemplifies this. Sensitivity involves fear and temptation, and all

nations, religions, industrial, and commercial establishments claim to

provide order based on fear and temptation. However, neither fear

nor temptation can be the basis of orderliness, as they are

unacceptable to humans. So, what should humans have? Values and

evaluation. There must be a method to recognise values and a

technique for evaluation. With these two things, the tradition of

continuous resolution will persist. Values and evaluation are

processes of understanding; they are not bodily or mechanical

processes. Currently, science asserts that everything is mechanical and

that feelings are insignificant. This mechanistic worldview forces

humans to struggle with fear and temptation, bringing us to a point

where the very sustainability of the Earth is in question.

A problem will not be resolved by introducing another problem or

by accumulating numerous problems. The eradication of problems

can only occur through resolution. There is no relief for us without

resolution.

In order to attain resolution, humans must develop a process to

establish orderliness through values and evaluation, rooted in

39 developed consciousness (humane consciousness). Success lies in

establishing orderliness with jeevan, its relationships, its satisfaction,

and its goals at the centre. If we neglect jeevan and construct systems

solely for the welfare of the body, it will only lead to disorder. What

'feels' right for the body is not always correct. The body, as an

entity, is not eternal; it undergoes change repeatedly, whereas

jeevan has eternal continuity. Therefore, we need to have the

wisdom to make decisions based on jeevan. Jeevan is in the same form

in all humans. Its powers and strengths are inexhaustible because the

jeevan atom remains unchanged in its constitution. The strength and

power of an entity manifest in its state and motion, respectively.

Every human acknowledges the continuity of their being, which is

due to presence of jeevan within them. Being itself is presence; the

study of reality occurs only in the present. Similarly, jeevan exists in

all humans in the same form, with identical strengths and powers.

Furthermore, since the goal of jeevan is happiness, all humans aspire

for happiness. These four facts must be kept in mind.

Jeevan is a constitutionally complete atom, a sentient unit. The

question arises: who creates it? The long-standing belief that

everything must have a creator and a destroyer persists, influencing

human thought as well. Humans, like this belief, think they can

create and destroy, which is a fundamental principle of science.

However, this mindset has led to significant frustrations. Some

nations claim they can create atom bombs, while others cannot,

making equality meaningless. True equality lies in the natural state of

40 existence, whereas the creation of bombs disrupts coexistence.

Existence naturally implies coexistence, and any deviation from this

natural order inevitably encounters resistance. Commerce, similarly,

has become profit-driven, perpetually pursuing 'more.' One person

thinks they have 'less,' another 'more,' leading to constant conflict.

Such an approach does not foster a healthy and happy human

existence. Therefore, for humans to live healthily and happily, they

must adopt values and evaluation guided by awakened consciousness.

The first step is understanding, the second step is honesty, the

third step is responsibility, and the fourth step is

participation.

Humans need to evidence their understanding through these four

steps. This understanding is categorised into three areas: knowledge

of jeevan, knowledge of the holistic view of coexistence, and

knowledge of humane conduct. I have already explained jeevan to

you. Jeevan is eternal, it aspires for happiness, and it can evidence

happiness only within the human tradition. The first step in this

process is to understand jeevan, which is termed “Jeevan Vidya”.

Jeevan is the bearer and the carrier of vidya. There are three parts in

the manifestation of vidya: vidya (knowledge), vidvata (learning), and

vidvan (the learned). Vidya (Knowledge): The entire coexistence is

the source of knowledge. Knowledge is inherently present within

coexistence. Jeevan is inseparable from coexistence. Vidvata

(Learning): This is the state of understanding, where jeevan accepts

41 coexistence. Vidvan (The Learned): A human who has become

learned. Every human is a combined form of jeevan and body.

What is the content of understanding? The entire existence in the

form of coexistence is the object of knowing, believing, and living.

Jeevan is the entity that is the carrier and bearer of learning, and the

human is the one who evidences it. A human being is a combined

form of jeevan and body. In this way, the significance of humans,

jeevan, and coexistence becomes clear. Existence is naturally in the

form of coexistence. Coexistence naturally leads to development.

Development is inherent to jeevan. Jeevan naturally tends to

awakening. For this, coexistence itself is the phenomenon, and jeevan

is the perceiver. The composition and decomposition activities in the

physicochemical world are mutually interdependent and eternally

present. There is no moment, day, or century when physicochemical

activities are absent. Jeevan is the perceiver of all these composition

and decomposition activities. It is jeevan that perceives and

understands; the body does not understand anything.

The part of the body devoid of the vitality of jeevan is termed as

numb. Sensations of cold or heat are not felt in such areas. For

instance, during surgery under anaesthesia, there is no perception of

pain from incisions or sutures. Thus, sensory perception occurs only

in those regions where jeevan maintains vitality. When jeevan seeks its

own fulfilment, it embarks on a quest for truth, meaning, and reality.

Therefore, jeevan is the basis of happiness. This is the reason we need

42 to understand jeevan. Everyone has this need—the rich, the poor, the

mighty, the weak, the old, and the young.

We discover another formula here: Jeevan Vidya refutes the

existential basis of class struggle. Instead, it recognises coexistence as

the foundation for universal well-being, the source of continuous

happiness for all, and evidence of resolution in life. These realisations

naturally arise upon understanding. In my view, humans want this

very knowledge, and they want to live according to this only. We can

live happily only in the togetherness of all. “Nothing is isolated” –

that is the principle. Attempting to find happ iness by severing our

relationship with the Earth is destined to fail. One cannot find

happiness by forsaking their relationship with water. If we cannot

become happy by leaving the relationship with material things, then

how will we become happy by leaving the relationship with jeevan?

How can we become so mechanistic? How can we be without

feelings? Reflect on how unsustainable such a life would be. When

we go to the market, we inquire about the value of every item –

vegetables, grains, gold, and so on. Who determines this value? Only

humans can. Since everything possesses value, humans themselves

should be valued. There was a crucial need to understand the value of

humans, yet we allocated value to everything else instead. We clung to

the value of those things where profit could be made, while

neglecting the value of humanity. By comprehending human values,

jeevan values, established values, and civic values, concerns about

profit and loss vanish. We would then live based on the usefulness

43 value, which will alleviate such a huge burden from the Earth. Profit

and loss constitute a relentless cycle that not only fails to secure

humans but also destroys everything in its path. Humans can break

free from this cycle only when they comprehend values. It is not

going to happen before that. This liberation cannot occur before this

understanding dawns. Despite our efforts, we have hit a wall, as

evidenced by communism and capitalism. Communism failed to

break free from the pursuit of profit and ended up striving for

national profit, while capitalism unabashedly prioritises profit.

Therefore, humans must grasp their values to emancipate themselves

from profit and loss. Fulfilling human values is imperative. How can

this be achieved? Human values are realised through understanding

Jeevan Vidya – i.e. comprehending existence in the form of

coexistence and embracing humane conduct with confidence. This,

in itself, constitutes understanding.

Only when we begin to embody human values do we become

capable, and consequently proficient, in doing what is 'right'. Until

then, we remain ensnared by various obsessions, unable to discern the

path towards righteousness.Humans need to understand jeevanand

humane conduct in coexistence in order to become wise. This itself is

Jeevan Vidya. Vidya has two parts – knowledge of jeevan, and the

knowledge of holistic view of coexistence. Jeevanis the carrier and

bearer of these both. The knowledge of jeevanmeans the process of a

jeevan understanding jeevan. The process of understanding existence

by a jeevanis called knowledge of the holistic view of coexistence. All

44 jeevans are identical, and therefore, the jeevans within all humans are

inherently alike. What defines this sameness? It becomes evident that

all jeevans share the same capacity for understanding jeevan,

evidencing knowledge, comprehending existence, and evidencing

coexistence.

The capacity for understanding does not reside in any part of the

body—whether hands, legs, ears, nose, eyes, brain, or heart. This

capacity solely exists within jeevan. Jeevan alone possesses the ability

to comprehend itself and coexistence; nothing else possesses this

capability. Thus, we deduce that the combined form of jeevan and

body is necessary for manifesting (evidencing) the understanding. It

would neither occur solely by the body nor solely by jeevan.

Evidence of understanding is exemplified through humans living in

orderliness and their participation in universal orderliness, which is

the embodiment of understanding itself. All of us want to live in

orderliness, and this naturally stems from jeevan; it is not an external

imposition upon us.

In the course of understanding coexistence, it becomes clear that

existence itself is coexistence, because nature, saturated (immersed,

soaked, and surrounded) in Omnipotence (Omnipresence),

constitutes the entire existence. Nature is in the form of entities that

can be counted. Humans are the ones who count. The countable

entities include all sentient and insentient nature.

45 There exists a simple formula: humans are happy with understanding

and unhappy as long as they dwell in ignorance or animal

consciousness. Throughout history, humanity has grappled with

various challenges. Initially, the struggle was against the forces of

nature and wild animals. Subsequently, people sought happiness

through practices such as penance, yoga, or asceticism, yet these

endeavours failed to yield any evidence of sustained happiness, and

the tradition of happiness could not be established. Another belief

arose that amassing material wealth and seeking comfort would bring

happiness, only to be disillusioned by its inefficacy. It became evident

upon reflection that understanding leads to resolution, and

resolution begets happiness. This understanding manifests as

righteous work and behaviour.

Humans are united in the right, and divided in the wrong. It is not

possible for you to agree or concur with my wrong, nor is it possible

for me to agree or concur with your wrong. That which is wrong is as

wrong for you as it is for me.We are united in the right, this I have

understood.

Our well-being becomes assured only in, from, and for the

understanding. It is only through understanding that we become

happy and prosperous. With understanding, we live orderly in the

present, and it is through understanding that we establish coexistence

as a tradition. There are four stages of happiness: living with

resolution, prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence. We become

happy when these four aspects are evident in our lives. Until we

46 achieve these four, we keep striving to establish the tradition of

understanding. In this pursuit, humans have engaged in various

practices such as chanting, penance, prayer, recitation of sciptures,

yoga, and yajna. We have amassed many material things, but this

hasn’t resulted in happiness for all. For universal happiness, humans

must become wise. Understanding can be instilled in everyone. The

first step is understanding existence, which consists of four orders.

Material Order: This includes soils, stones, gems, metals, etc., all of

which exhibit definite conduct. Biological order: This encompasses

all trees, plants, vegetation, medicinal herbs, etc., which also

demonstrate their respective definite conducts. Animal Order: This

includes all animals and birds, excluding humans, and these too show

inherent orderliness. Knowledge Order: This comprises only

humans, who are yet to achieve orderliness. Consider this: the most

developed order (knowledge order) is lagging behind all others. What

does this imply? It implies that humans are suffering because they

have not yet attained the developed form of consciousness.

Therefore, our consciousness needs to develop to reflect our evolved

status.

Each entity in existence evidences orderliness in the form of its

conduct. Humans will also evidence orderliness through their

conduct. This is the principle that all of us need to verify. As we go

about this verification, we must first understand the entity within us

that actually understands. Then, we must understand the entity that

lives based on that understanding. Finally, we must understand what

47 we will accomplish by this understanding. This is the extent of

human potential. Humans are counted in the knowledge order.

What is the basis for considering humans in the knowledge order?

Even within the realm of animal consciousness, humans work and

behave according to what they believe they’ve understood.

Everyone has the capacity of believing. Even when one is living in

animal consciousness, they don't truly know but only believe, yet

they still make claims of knowing. This is a contradiction because it is

not possible to verify universal well-being while living in animal

consciousness. This contradiction is present in deluded humans.

Ninety-nine percent of people consider themselves to be merely

bodies, and this delusion has led to various difficulties. As a result,

humanity has been plagued by these difficulties and now aspires to

liberate itself from them. This program aims to address that

aspiration.

Only humans among the four orders of nature cannot attain

happiness without understanding and resolution. The material order

is regulated by structural conformity, while the biological order is

regulated by seed conformity. The animal order is regulated by

species conformity. The evidence of regulation manifests as

orderliness and definite conduct. Every unit of nature, except

humans, exhibits definite conduct. Humans also require definite

conduct, which they achieve through sanskar-conformity. Sanskar,

manifested as developed consciousness, is the basis of understanding.

Humane conduct is the evidence of this understanding. When

48 humans become wise, they live in orderliness, and their conduct is

humane. However, when they fail to live in orderliness, their conduct

is deemed inhumane. This distinction gives us the definition of

humane and inhumane conduct. Subsequently, we realise whether

we need it or not. Humans have a natural tendency towards what

they need. This is the path for humans to become awakened.

Jeevan is neither born nor does it die; it is the body that gets formed

and deformed. Jeevan wants to drive the human body according to its

own natural way – which is the understanding and program of being

happy. All animals only exhibit the hope of living by the way of

species-conformity. However, humans aspire to live happily, and they

encounter difficulties when they attempt to live according to

species-conformity. That is the essence of it. This needs to be

properly understood and evidenced. Understanding itself is to be

evidenced. When, having grasped the understanding from you, I am

able to convey it to others, only then does your understanding

become evident. This is how understanding flows in tradition.

Ignorance cannot flow in tradition. The object of understanding

doesn’t vary. Any variation occurs in its expression; thus, with each

successive generation, it becomes more robust and refined. The path

of righteousness keeps becoming ever sharper and more accessible.

This is necessary for all humans. Hence, only a human possessing

understanding can correctly impart their wisdom to the succeeding

generation, thus finding satisfaction for themselves and for the future

generation

49 Humans are sanskar-conforming units. Sanskar is the combined form

of understanding, honesty, responsibility, and participation. Since

wrongs are not acceptable to anyone, they do not become sanskar.

No one accepts wrongs but remains ensnared by them. Even if a

person has committed a thousand wrongs, those wrongs remain

unacceptable to them. Because wrongs are not acceptable to anyone,

no one passes them on to the next generation. Thus, the tradition of

senselessness (wrongs) does not form. These examples lead to the

conclusion that understanding is the foundation of tradition. The

focal point for understanding is the identicality of humane

consciousness among humans. The focus of identicality is jeevan.

Constitutional completeness and inexhaustible strengths and powers

are the identicalities in every jeevan. Regardless of the extent of hope,

thought, or desire, my capacity for them remains intact. The

inexhaustible strengths and powers in jeevan couldn't exist if its

constitution were subject to change. This is the logical reasoning for

accepting the constitutional completeness of jeevan.

The understanding that has been accepted in me is verified through

my behaviour, work, and participation in systems. I have repeatedly

verified it in my behaviour and work, and found that my living is

orderly in the form of resolution and prosperity. However, universal

orderliness is yet to be established in human tradition. My living in

the form of an indivisible society itself serves as evidence in human

tradition of my having understood reality as it is in existence, which

further enhances realisation. This realisation keeps strengthening

50 over time. This paves the way for realisation-based living. In

conclusion, upon attaining understanding, humans live in

orderliness through a realisation-based approach. The orderliness of

the animal order is through species-conformance, the biological order

is through seed-conformance, and the material order is through

constitution-conformance.

We can conclude that understanding is definite and it pertains to

living with developed consciousness. The bearer and carrier of

understanding is definite; therefore, the evidence of understanding is

also definite. Jeevan itself becomes wise. Jeevan is the entity that

understands, and the evidence of understanding occurs only within

human tradition because the fully developed brain is found only in

the human body. The evidence of understanding will not be found in

any other (animal) species. Coexistence encompasses

complementariness, evolution, development progression,

development and awakening. The method for understanding all

these points is inherent only in humans. The potential for this

understanding is also inherent only in humans.

The fundamental issue in understanding existence is that existence is

nature saturated in Omnipotence. Nature and Omnipotence are

found to be thoroughly intertwined with one another, eternally

inseparable, continuously extant and present. There is no method to

separate nature from Omnipresence, nor is there any purpose in such

separation, as they cannot be separated. Thus, imagining something

that does not exist within existence yields no tangible results. The

51 task at hand is to comprehend and validate what exists. Existence

manifests itself across the four orders.

If we fail to evidence understanding, we will neither be able to live in

the orderliness of family nor in the orderliness of society, and will end

up suffering everywhere. The human population on Earth has

surpassed seven billion, yet our orderly way of living has not yet

materialised. Whether the population grows or diminishes, it has

nothing to do with the attainment of understanding. What is the

purpose of human tradition? It is to evidence resolution,

prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence. Coexistence means

living with complementarity. Fearlessness is trust in the

present. Prosperity is producing in excess of our family’s needs.

Resolution is living with justice.

Human endeavours through idealism and materialism could not

achieve the understanding. The root cause of this is our failure to

understand existence in the form of coexistence. We erred in

understanding jeevan and its awakening within coexistence, as a

result the tradition of understanding could not be established.

Without such a tradition, how could humans learn to live in

orderliness? In the absence of understanding, we have not managed

to live judiciously with fellow humans and lawfully with the rest of

nature (animal, biological, and material order) in a balanced way.

This is why humans have continued to destroy their natural

surroundings.

52 Humans have not been able to find justice anywhere. When the chief

justices of high courts were questioned about it, they responded, 'We

do not administer justice; we merely render judgments.' If the judicial

courts themselves are unaware of justice, can they truly be called halls

of justice? Especially when these very courts instruct you to speak the

truth. What truth can be expected from such courts?"

Similarly, what tasks does the administration perform besides

searching for errors and crimes, and then attempting to prevent them

by committing more errors and crimes? All personnel in the

government machinery are deployed to these tasks alone. The

essential element for human awakening is understanding. If

understanding reaches every human being, then humanity shall be

able to live justly. With justice comes prosperity, fearlessness, and

coexistence naturally. Without living justly, resolution cannot be

achieved. Therefore, justice is the backbone of humaneness. Justice is

first evidenced in a wise family, then in society, and finally across the

whole Earth as universal orderliness. Living justly ensures that

humans remain satisfied, happy, and resolved. Their trust in the

present becomes firmer, and their behaviour continuously refines. All

of these are accomplished spontaneously by living with justice. It is

said that one achieves these through the accumulation of virtue,

which I now understand to mean wisdom. In the tradition of

wisdom, humans spontaneously manifest their potential, ability, and

receptivity. Potential means the activity of carrying, whether it be

delusion or awakening. Delusion dissipates naturally upon

53 awakening. Humans are sanskar-conformance units. Tradition is the

source of understanding or delusion. The traits of tradition are

instilled in a human child from birth. Thereafter through their

diligence and quest, they become liberated from delusion upon

attaining wisdom. Liberation from delusion signifies living in

alignment with jeevan's awakening. The education we have received

from tradition so far is primarily focused on living in alignment with

the body, akin to animals. This emphasis is evident in the obsession

for profit, sex, and consumption fostered by such education.

However, human nature is fundamentally distinct from that of

animals. Humans are multidimensional expressions, seeking

resolution and prosperity in ways unparalleled by any animal, plant,

or stone. While animals instinctively collect what they find without

hoarding, humans exhibit a wilful tendency towards comfort and

accumulation, driven by a lust for over-consumption. Consequently,
