comfort and accumulation have supplanted resolution and

orderliness as the primary goals of our lives. Our perspective has

become confined to pleasure, health, and profit, resulting in ongoing

suffering, struggle, and oppression. The only way out of this

difficulty is to understand jeevan’s awakening, coexistence and

humane conduct.

Humans are the most developed entities in existence, both as jeevan

and in bodily form. Jeevanuses the body to manifest its existence

and awakening. While keeping the body alive, jeevan falls into the

delusion that the body itself is jeevan by living in animal

54 consciousness. However, this cycle eventually restarts with jeevan

incarnating into a new body, driven by the imperative to manifest

itself. This perpetual cycle of birth and death is a matter of distress.

It is not a matter of virtue or sin but rather one of understanding or

ignorance. Since understanding is inherited from tradition, it must

be integral to tradition itself. The emancipation of the whole world

does not depend solely on one person becoming wise; such notions

only engender fear and helplessness. In the realm of humane

conduct, every individual can live with rightfully owned wealth,

marital faithfulness, and kindness in work and behaviour. Right-use

and protection of body, mind and wealth are ensured by such living.

When these elements are harmonised, justice - manifested through

relationships, values, evaluation, and mutual satisfaction - becomes

self-evident.

In this way, humane conduct is explained as the combined form of

values, character, and ethics. The right-use and protection of

resources in the form of body, mind, and wealth constitute ethics.

Values are realised through the recognition of relationships. For

example, when someone recognises their relationship with their

father, mother, or guru in terms of orderliness, values naturally flow,

resulting in the fulfilment of those values. Where relationships are

not recognised, there is no flow of values.

Consider a scenario where someone is sitting alone in a train

compartment, and a stranger enters. The individual who was seated

initially instinctively stretches out their hands and legs, reluctant to

55 share the space. However, if a familiar person enters, they may even

offer their seat willingly. Hence, the recognition of relationships is

paramount. The study of relationships is guided by their respective

purposes; nurturing defines the mother-child relationship, while

protection characterises the father-child relationship. Once all the

relationships are recognised, humans no longer make mistakes in

these contexts. Conversely, in the absence of such recognition,

mistakes are inevitable.

56 It is evident from observing the propaganda of the prevailing systems

of the State and Religion that these have been designed for criminals.

Both of these systems are engaged in the redemption of criminals in

their own way. However, neither of these systems has been able to

impart understanding to humans. Every human being desires to

become wise and honest, yet these systems have not been able to

show the path of honesty. Similarly, every human aspires to become

responsible, but these systems have failed to instil the purpose of

responsibility in tradition. People have expressed desires for universal

wellbeing, family happiness, and similar aspirations. We have all

echoed such slogans. However, mere utterance or repetition does not

lead to finding the path.

The same book that speaks of universal wellbeing also declares the

world to be an illusion and advocates seeking refuge in God as the

real father and mother. Yet, no tangible good comes from it. After

seeking refuge in the 'real mother and father,' no human is found. So,

whose good will occur and where? These narratives serve no real

purpose. It is through wisdom that the purpose of humanity

becomes clear. Purpose is inherent in all relationships. But what is

this purpose? It is solely about achieving resolution, prosperity,

fearlessness, and coexistence. The purpose of all relationships is

intricately linked to these goals, thus forming a tradition aligned with

them. This tradition can only be one of understanding; ignorance

cannot sustain an unbroken tradition. Consequently, no tradition

aimed at universal wellbeing has been established thus far.

57 Those produced by the current education system consider themselves

the epitome of intelligence, while viewing the rest of the world as

stupid. Millions of such graduates emerge annually. How do we

impart understanding to each one of them? Where will we find

enough doctors to fix them?

No one accepts anything until they have understood it themselves. I

am a testament to this truth. I was surrounded by ved-murtis in my

family, neighbourhood, and village, yet they could not make me read

the Vedas because I did not want to read. However, every individual

on Earth desires to become wise. On this basis, there is a complete

possibility that every human can become wise. It is on this premise

that I initiated this movement. It began with a sincere ambition to

impart understanding to every human being. Through this

movement, those who have gained understanding have found solace,

and qualities we deem humane have blossomed within them.

The essence of ethics is deploying resources in the form of body,

mind and wealth towards purpose. It is called the right-use.

Right-use happens in two ways: - 1. Deploying body, mind and

wealth towards production and seva, 2. Devoting body, mind and

wealth with relationships towards realisation of their purpose.When

resources are rightly used, they become secure, and whatever purpose

they are used for also becomes secure. This is what we mean by

right-use and security. When we allocate our resources—body, mind,

and wealth—towards resolution, prosperity, and orderliness, with

trust in the present and fostering coexistence, they become secure.

58 This results in the right-use of our wealth. There won’t be security

without right-use, and there can't be right-use without security.

Right-use and security of resources lead to eternal wellbeing. The

inherent need to deploy our body, mind, and wealth towards

righteousness is meant for our awakening.

Human beings are the only entities in existence capable of wisdom.

Humans are a combination of jeevan and body. Human bodies

follow the lineage tradition, while jeevan exists naturally in existence

as a constitutionally complete entity, with no human contribution to

its creation. The human body, however, is a product of human

tradition. This is how it is provisioned in existence. The union of

jeevan and body is necessary for jeevan to manifest its awakening.

Human bodies have the provision to evidence understanding, a

feature not present in animal bodies. Therefore, humans are

recognised as sanskar-conformance entities. Apart from humans, all

three orders in nature are mutually complementary. Now, it is

imperative for humans to embrace complementariness. For humans

to live in harmony, complementariness is essential; this cannot be

achieved through individualism or hedonism. The two ideologies of

materialism and asceticism in the past led humans towards

individualism. Materialism leads humans towards hedonism,

resulting in individualism. Asceticism, on the other hand, is

inherently individualistic. Both of these ideologies failed to provide a

blueprint for societal formation and instead proved to be detrimental

to society. However, humans yearn to live in society. They desire to

59 live in coexistence, prosperity, and resolution. It is the responsibility

of humankind to achieve these three objectives: coexistence,

prosperity, and resolution.

Understanding naturally leads to responsibility, and taking up

responsibility makes us participants in family and society. This leads

to our evidencing the universality of being human. There is a need to

establish such a magnificent tradition of humankind. Every human

being hopes for orderliness, aspires for orderliness, and, according to

me, even desires orderliness. However, this desire often takes a

backseat to other priorities. As a result, the desire for orderliness

remains weak, and humans find themselves unable to fully commit to

it. They become helpless due to living in animal consciousness.

Therefore, what is the solution? We should focus on educating those

who are ready to understand immediately. Through them, we should

practice humane education in educational institutions and instill

sanskar in children. As sanskar is instilled in children, their homes

and families will naturally undergo a transformation. Thus, there is a

need for the humanisation of education. Making education

meaningful will pave the way for an orderly society, which is our

second plan.

The units of material order, biological order, and animal order

are complementary to humans. However, humans becoming

complementary to them is still under consideration. This gap

60 must be filled. Only then will we get the evidence of human

living in orderliness.

The values of awakened jeevan are: happiness, peace, contentment,

and bliss. Human goals are accomplished by realising jeevan values.

These goals are resolution, prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence.

When human goals are evidenced, jeevan values are also evidenced.

Resolution = Happiness. We realise happiness wherever we are

resolved, and we suffer wherever we are unresolved. Thereafter, we

realise peace while evidencing resolution and prosperity in the family.

We realise contentment by living orderly in society. We realise bliss in

the course of evidencing our understanding.

As we achieve these goals, understanding becomes ingrained in

human tradition, enabling us to realise happiness, peace,

contentment, and bliss, respectively.

61 Jeevan possesses inexhaustible strengths and powers. Therefore, once

resolution is attained, we can continuously manifest and evidence it,

while the fulfilment of jeevan remains intact. Jeevan’s state activities

are in the form of strengths, and its motion activities are in the form

of powers. The motion activities of jeevan are evidenced in their

mutuality with one another. The state activities of jeevan are realised

within oneself. We realise whether or not we became satisfied with all

that we tasted and whether or not we reached a definite conclusion

from all the deliberation we did.

Further, I attained realisation after revelation (sakshatkar) and

definitive understanding (avdharna bodh) of truth, thereupon

contemplated (chintan) through this enlightenment (bodh). I keep

examining the purpose of my actions based on this essential

understanding. We will have to do this examining, there is no other

way. Satisfaction of jeevanat these five levels paves the way for

continuous happiness. This itself has been termed as happiness,

peace, contentment and bliss. The evidence in these five levels in

jeevangets established as the grandeur of self-governance in human

living. The self-governance is the grandeur of humans upon attaining

humaneness, or orderly living. Self-governance is the self-inspired

orderly living, which is the manifestation of humane conduct. The

grandeur of human awakening is in realising their relationships at the

level of individual, family, society, nature, and universal orderliness.

We come to trust in the present only through the process of realising

values in our relationships. Without recognising our relationships,

62 we cease to inhabit the present, instead retreating into a past devoid

of presence. Yet, we cannot dwell in the past. Thus, we cast our

thoughts towards the future, which similarly lacks presence.

Consequently, humans find themselves adrift, lacking a tether to life's

purpose, and thus wander aimlessly. No one desires such aimlessness,

yet tradition fails to provide direction and purpose. The evidence of

tradition will emerge only when every individual can attain

enlightenment through consciousness development value education.

The understanding can manifest as humaneness in every human’s

conduct. The grandeur and magnificence of humans is in making

understanding prevail. It is with this grandeur that humans can

achieve a tradition of continuous happiness. They can achieve

harmony in their interaction with the animal world, plant world and

mineral world, making their use and right-use while being grateful

for their complementariness, thereby living purposefully.

The harmony with humans is as a relationship, values, evaluation and

mutual satisfaction. We choose satisfaction over dissatisfaction. Every

human, in the anticipation of satisfaction, evidences coexistence

through resolution, prosperity, trust in the present, and living in

orderliness. Existence is the ultimate truth, since this itself has eternal

continuity in the form of coexistence. Coexistence is continuously in

effect, as a result there is emergence of development and awakening.

The development progression is as continuous activity of

physicochemical reality. How many jeevanatoms are to be is

63 determined by the way of coexistence, it is not the doing of deluded

humans.

Existence has manifested all the four orders naturally, which has no

human contribution. Humans could not evidence

complementariness with the rest of nature, instead they have only

been exploiting it. It begs the question: how can humanity hope to

find happiness through exploitation? This is a matter worth

pondering. Across nations, sects, religions, and even within families,

the prevailing belief is that happiness can be attained through

exploitation. Both the state and society uphold this belief,

considering exploitation as the only means to human happiness. This

mindset persists to this day. Even science aligns with this notion,

asserting that human survival hinges on struggle and exploitation.

Survival here refers to survival of one’s own kins. Struggle implies -

might is right. The prevailing belief suggests that development is

synonymous with struggle. A nation's development is often

measured by its capacity to wage wars, engage in commerce, and

exploit resources. However, the truth is that development is attained

only by a nation that has become awakened - one that embodies

orderliness, resolution, prosperity, confidence, and understanding of

coexistence.

There is a difference in the way jeevanunderstands jeevan, and the

way jeevanunderstands existence. As far as material things are

concerned, we recognise them upon experimentation based on their

usefulness. We recognise usefulness in the form of common and

64 special aspirations. The common aspirations are food, shelter and

clothing. The special aspirations are telecommunication and

transportation. Most of these have been discovered and are being

produced. There have been efforts to make these commonly

accessible commercially. Commercial methods, however, are always

with anticipation of profit.

65 The identification of our common and special aspirations is derived

from the jeevan's analysis activity. Once these are identified, we

engage in their production, leading to the realisation of prosperity.

As prosperity dawns, we begin to live in a state of orderliness. Hence,

it is imperative to cultivate self-reliance in our students, and

thereafter develop their tendency for evidence in the family and living

in universal orderliness. It is good fortune of humans to evidence at

these three levels. Its inherent need in humans is the one and only

basis to actualise this good fortune. When this need gets identified

then it would be natural for humans to evidence themselves after

diligently studying this proposal.

So far, we have tried to understand - what is understanding? Who

understands? What is the content of understanding? The entity that

understands is ‘jeevan’. The content of understanding is ‘existence’,

‘jeevan’, and ‘humane conduct’ only. In the journey of

comprehending existence, we need to understand development, as

well as the physicochemical composition and decomposition

processes. These processes are inherent in existence, manifesting as

material order and biological order. These undergo continuous

transformation from one state to another. For instance, trees and

plants naturally wither over time, transforming into soil—a

phenomenon known as transformability, which characterises the

perpetual flux of the physicochemical realm. Similarly, the formation

and eventual demise of animal and human bodies follow a cyclical

pattern. Bodies are conceived and take shape in the womb, only to

66 return to the elements upon death, contributing to the cycle of soil,

air, and water.

The entity which understands, jeevan, remains the same forever. In

humans, jeevanis the only entity that understands. Existence has

been understood in the form of coexistence only. It is only with the

co-existential outlook that we become capable of living in orderliness

in every situation. Living in orderliness is the goal of humans, living

in orderliness itself is happiness. Jeevansuffers from problems while

living in disorder. Consequently, the search for resolution becomes

inevitable. Jeevanhas an inherent tendency to continuously search

and explore. It is not just in jeevan, exploration goes on even in the

insentient atoms. This is the cause of transformation in the

insentient nature. Everywhere, there exists a natural inclination

towards coexistence. This inclination is what leads atomic particles to

assemble into atoms, atoms to combine into molecules, and

molecules to combine into molecular forms. In this way, humans can

understand the being of infinite planets and celestial bodies in

existence. The basic form of diversity in the insentient nature lies in

the differentiation of particles comprising atoms. These distinct

atomic structures, each with its defined status in nature, give rise to

diversity in their arrangements. For instance, the biological order

exhibits a multitude of compositions. These compositions, inherent

to the entities, naturally exist in their respective forms, participating

in coexistence. The substances taking these forms are also

embodiments of coexistence. Thus, the entirety of existence, with its

67 manifestations, is grounded in this principle. Humans, too, are a part

of existence.

Humans are inseparable from coexistence; they cannot detach

themselves from it. The more they try to escape, the deeper their

turmoil grows. Every individual yearns for resolution, driving them

on an endless quest. Each person holds the right to pursue harmony

within the framework of existence. As every human being lives by

seeking, the meaning of free will becomes clear. Life's purpose

converges on a singular goal: happiness. Humans seek to live with

happiness. There is only one path to happiness i.e. achieving jeevan’s

and human’s objective. Jeevan’s objective is accomplished with

understanding. Jeevanbecomes satisfied with understanding, and a

satisfied jeevanalone is capable of sustaining the evidence of the

human objectives of resolution, prosperity, fearlessness and

coexistence. This itself is the evidence of living in orderliness. As one

lives in orderliness, these four goals are achieved. Such a human

tradition is beneficent for one another. Imparting understanding to

another itself is benevolence, whereby the meaning of coexistence

gets actualised in the form of tradition. In human tradition,

orderliness entails maintaining coexistence in the present. Anything

that disrupts coexistence also disturbs orderliness. Due to their

imaginativeness and free will, deluded humans can cause any kind of

disturbance. For instance, significant damage has been inflicted upon

the Earth. They didn’t know what difficulties could arise from this

disturbance, and when they came to know, there was no available

68 remedy. Humans keep searching and exploring owing to their

imaginativeness and free will, but this search and exploration is

meaningful only when it is for orderliness, and for achieving

resolution, prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence. Understanding

leads humans to achieve:

1.Self-confidence

2.Respect for Excellence

3.Balance in Talent and Personality

4.Sociability in Behaviour

5.Self-reliance in Vocation

These can be called merits. Humans become social with these merits.

Evidencing understanding in living itself is ‘learning’. Only humans

could become ‘learned’ among all the existence. While there is a

continuous search in every unit of nature, the learning is possible

only in humans.

We have described four activities in humans here – knowing,

believing, recognising, and fulfilling. Among these, recognising and

fulfilling are inherent in every entity of nature. Every entity of nature

recognises another; that is why it fulfils. An atomic particle too

recognises another, and as a result, these particles abide in orderliness.

They cohabit and function with one another, thus manifesting

coexistence. Similarly, starting from molecules to planets, the entities

of nature recognise one another and fulfil accordingly. All units of

69 material order, biological order, and animal order also recognise one

another and fulfil, which is evident in the form of complementariness

in nature.

Humans, however, could not be satisfied with mere recognising and

fulfilling, and doubts arose within them. Humans have two

additional activities – knowing and believing. Humans become

satisfied with recognising and fulfilling only on the basis of knowing

and believing. Knowing and believing are only of meaning and

purpose. Humans can become social only in the course of knowing

and believing. In the absence of knowing and believing, one cannot

become social nor can they evidence coexistence.

The activities of jeevancould basically be seen in five parts. Each part

has two activities in the form of state and motion respectively. For

example, every jeevanhas hope (asha) wherein there are two activities

– taste (asvadan) and selection (chayan). What we choose according

to our taste is the selection activity. We taste, which is also an activity.

The part of jeevanwhere both these activities happen is called mun.

For selection activity, humans have imagined what all is needed for

taste. They have accumulated a great deal for this, and are busy in

accumulating even more. So far, we have worked for comfort and

accumulation. The reason being, the more we lagged in

understanding (knowing and believing) the purpose of comfort and

accumulation, the more helpless we became for these. We could not

find the point of satisfaction of comfort and accumulation anywhere.

70 However, when we understand the practical purpose of our material

accumulation, we learn that food, shelter and clothing are for

nourishment and protection of body, while telecommunication and

transportation are for social participation. All these things have

become available, but humans haven’t become satisfied based on

comfort and accumulation. This is a huge irony.

Two other activities of jeevanare deliberation (tulan) and analysis

(vishleshan). Jeevanperforms analysis activity based on its capability.

All analyses are ultimately for recognising purposes. The

fundamental purpose of humans is to evidence resolution,

prosperity, fearlessness and coexistence in living. The opposite path is

pursuit of consumption and over-consumption, where humans

won’t find any stability.

At present, science concludes that all humans will be dead after some

time and Earth will get destroyed. That is bound to happen if we go

on like this. Thinking from the way Earth has evolved, humans

emerged only after the planet had become fully enriched and

habitable for them. Gradually the opportunity of awakening became

available to humans living in animal consciousness. Instead of

becoming awakened, they moved towards consumption and

over-consumption. By making consumption and over-consumption

their way of life, they entered into an endless pursuit of comfort and

accumulation. The Earth does not have enough resources to satisfy

everyone's lust for comfort and accumulation. Therefore, sooner or

later, this lust will lead to human ruin. All objects of comfort and

71 accumulation need to be aligned with the human purpose – i.e.,

towards the nourishment-protection of the body and social

participation. Moving towards social participation leads to

participation in an indivisible society and universal orderliness. As

humans live based on these premises, they become capable of living

with resolution-prosperity and happiness-peace. In this way, the goal

of jeevan is to evidence human awakening in existence. In this way,

the goal of jeevanis to evidence human awakening in existence. Its

success is based on the fact that every human wants to live in

orderliness. While in delusion, the basis of order is fear and

temptation. Upon awakening, orderliness is with the recognition of

values, evaluation, and mutual satisfaction. There is a need to develop

understanding for it.

May there be universal well-being!

72

The True form of Jeevan

Jeevan is the inseparable form of mun, vritti, chitta, buddhi, and

atma, as these never separate from one another. Mun has two

functions: selection (chayan) and taste (asvadan). Vritti has two

functions: analysis (vishleshan) and deliberation (tulan). Chitta has

two functions: visualisation (chitran) and contemplation (chintan).

Buddhi has two functions: resolve (sankalp) and enlightenment

(bodh). Atma has two functions: authenticity (pramanikta) and

realisation (anubhav). Every jeevan continuously operates through

these ten activities. Jeevan, with these ten activities, is evidenced in

either a state of delusion or awakening. In a deluded state, jeevan is

inspired by sensitivity, and only four and a half out of its ten activities

are effective due to animal consciousness. The remaining activities

lack the substance for understanding, resulting in internal conflict

within jeevan. These four and a half activities are selection, taste,

analysis, visualisation, and half of deliberation. Taste and selection

occur based on sensitivity, where one chooses what is pleasant to the

hands, feet, nose, ears, eyes, tongue, etc., and avoids what is

unpleasant. Deliberation, based on sensitivity, operates from the

perspective of pleasure, health, and profit. In the same vein, analysis

and visualisation activities are also performed accordingly. In

summary, we become ready to live while being identified with bodily

sensations. This is called a “deluded jeevan.” This leads to

continuous internal conflict, with constant dilemmas about whether

73 something is right or wrong, more or less. This mentality resembles

that of primitive humans, though only material things have

increased. Awakening the remaining five and a half activities of

jeevan, which happens through understanding, is essential for

developing a humane mentality.

The four and a half activities of jeevanare sufficient for recognising

and fulfilling the five senses and four instincts, where humans live

like an animal or a demon. It is not possible to live humanely with

only four and a half activities. Such living doesn’t result in

satisfaction. The main issue now is to evidence all ten activities of

jeevanin behaviour, as “awakening”. Manifesting partial activities

would not be awakening. For example, a healthy body is when all the

five sense organs and the five action organs are functioning properly

with mutual coordination. If someone’s hands or legs don’t work

then we will call that person a cripple. We won’t call that person

healthy.

Awakening cannot happen unless and until we connect our activities

of recognising and fulfilling, with our activities of knowing and

believing. Until now, humans have evidenced jeevan’s four and a half

activities through recognising and fulfilling sensory desires. The

remaining activities of jeevanare evidenced in behaviour, which is the

basis of awakening. This will happen only by way of knowing and

believing. Nature, apart from humans, remains regulated in course of

recognising and fulfilling wherein it functions according to its laws,

this way they are in orderliness.

74 The maximum that can happen with sensitivity gets achieved in the

animal world. Had that been the final destination, there is no need

for humans to exist. Nothing is purposeless in existence. Existence as

a whole is in the form of a synergistic, harmonious and rhythmic

orderliness. Each motion, each state, each order in existence is

interwoven meaningfully. This meaningfulness is in the form of

conduct in orderliness and participation in universal orderliness. In

awakened jeevan- enlightenmentand resolve activities are based on

realisation and authenticity, and thereafter the contemplation and

visualisation activities also start functioning accordingly. The same

becomes the basis for deliberation, analysis, taste and selection

activities. Currently, in our delusion, we perceive sensitivity as the

paramount attribute for thinking and planning about anything.

However, awakening is rooted solely in values and evaluation. Our

entire lifestyle has been constructed around sensitivity. In this

lifestyle, everything necessary for survival is valued except for humans

themselves. It encompasses the animal world, plant world, and

mineral world. We are all too familiar with how we humans have

exploited these resources, relentlessly pursuing our own success at the

expense of others, resulting in imbalance. Earth is suffering from our

relentless pursuit of comfort and accumulation. Now, there looms a

question of whether it's still possible to salvage Earth. Humans will

have to stop the crimes they have been committing with Earth and

they will have to understand the way of living without crime. The

freedom from crime cannot happen from the ideas presented by

75 science so far, which have entered into art and education as well. That

path leads to a dead-end, destruction of Earth, and conflict among

humans.

Several major nations have united to form the United Nations

Organisation (UNO), which has convened numerous conventions. It

remains undecided whether the right to militarization should reside

with this union, individual nations, or if it should not exist at all.

Should wars exist in any form? Similarly, our education system

undergoes quarterly reviews. Despite multiple reviews, the ideal

education for humans remains undecided.

In my observation, every human child is inherently inclined towards

doing what is right and seeks justice. They speak the truth. However,

as they grow up, they learn to lie because we have created an

environment where living without lying seems impossible. Lies

pervade the commercial world. State rule is founded on deception.

Even education fails to nurture truth. What recourse is there for

humans in such a situation? In this way, the daily routines and

behaviour of people get shaped by their circumstances. Humans have

not reached any definite goal under these conditions, nor will they

ever in the future. It is imperative to come out of this crisis, but that

will happen only when humans become wise. When that happens,

their way of life will be characterised by humane conduct.

Values and evaluation in humane conduct are founded on the

principle of coexistence. Realising values does not require the

76 establishment of laboratories or engagement in warfare. Knowing

and believing the purpose of relationships is essential for recognising

and fulfilling them towards indivisible society and universal

orderliness. Without knowing and believing the purpose, recognising

and fulfilling go astray. For instance, we overlooked the purpose of

our relationship with the Earth. We failed to understand the purpose

of the environment. Consequently, we could not grasp the totality of

the Earth and its environment. This lack of understanding led to the

catastrophic collapse of our planet. It is imperative to understand

unequivocally that if humankind is to survive on this Earth, then this

proposal outlines the necessary course correction for humanity.

Due to delusion, humans have lived for sensory gratification rather

than with conscious awareness, leaving them unsatisfied. A

dissatisfied person does whatever they feel like doing. Our entire task

is to transform dissatisfaction into satisfaction, which we call

'awakening'. Satisfaction will come through understanding, which is

the eternal source of fulfilment. Jeevan never dies; when it gains

understanding and satisfaction, this state continues forever. We have

seen all these things. Based on this, the proposal is that

understanding is the right of every human. Every individual can

research this. In my opinion, humanity can prosper and create its

future moments with complete resolution.

Biological cells decompose into the soil and turn into fertiliser. The

natural arrangement of food for food is an intrinsic process in nature.

Fertilisers are formed naturally this way. Biological cells are created,

77 and the structures made from these cells decompose back into the

soil, becoming fertiliser. Human emergence on Earth occurred only

after this soil fertility was established. Since humans appeared, they

began exploiting forests. With the advent of the scientific age, the

exploitation extended to minerals. Excessive exploitation of both

minerals and vegetation has depleted the Earth’s fertility and the

levels of life-giving oxygen.

Now, to the scientists who believe they are benefitting the world by

producing chemical fertilisers, I suggest that the natural process of

fertiliser formation is the only way to preserve Earth’s fertility. Rivers

carry and deposit unnecessary materials from the Earth's surface into

the oceans, maintaining balance. Dense vegetation and forests on

Earth’s surface are crucial for this balance. Instead, we humans tend

to create additional problems while attempting to solve existing ones.

One problem cannot cover up another problem. Even if a minor

problem is masked by a larger one, it remains unresolved.

This is not a complaint or condemnation; rather, it is a factual

account of past events and a proposal for reconsideration. It simply

describes the current state and the urgent need for change.

This proposal, in summary, aims to evidence all ten activities of

jeevan in human tradition. It seeks to evidence understanding

through consciousness development and value education. This

involves knowing, believing, recognising, and fulfilling. The point of

satisfaction for knowing and believing is awakening itself, which is

78 evidenced by resolution, prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence.

This itself is the evidence of realisation. Therefore, every human can

make their life meaningful by living based on realisation.

Another benefit of this proposal is that it has no place for priesthood

or power-centric rule. It is also free from the idea that only one

person will liberate everyone. Each individual can liberate themselves

from delusion by attaining understanding.

The notion that the liberation of one person would lead to the

liberation of the whole world has proven insufficient, as we have seen.

In this proposal, whoever understands it will become liberated. The

holy scriptures offer numerous assurances, yet not a single person on

Earth has emerged as evidence of their teachings. What, then, is the

solution for us? Anything that cannot be integrated into tradition is

of no value.

The tradition can only be successful when it is based on

understanding, where humans live with humaneness. The tradition

of understanding can be established through education, and the

tradition of right living comes about by way of family, society, and

systems. I too discovered my way of living on the basis of

understanding. Living based on understanding must entail

resolution and orderliness.

Humans don’t become social without evidencing justice. Without

justice, humans form sects that are rife with arguments and disputes.

In such sects, revolts, rebellions, conflicts and wars inevitably occur.

79 Given this prevalence of conflict and exploitation, can we truly

consider humans to be social? If we justify sectarian struggle, it could

eventually lead every individual to resort to violence and war. Why,

then, do we restrict that possibility? Therefore, we must reconsider

our approach. Properly understanding this prompts us to reflect on

our actions, as what we have done thus far has proven insufficient.

Thinking is the inherent nature of humans. Every individual can

think and search. We must find satisfaction in our own search and

also strive to be a source of satisfaction for others.

What should be done to start from here? First, understanding should

become accessible to all through education and sanskar. We need to

adopt the art of living with understanding - which encompasses how

we coexist with Earth, water, air, plants, animals, and humans. We

cannot exclude any; we must live in harmony with all of these. Every

human being inherently claims that they can realise and evaluate.

This claim is a natural, spontaneous zeal within human beings; no

one accepts imposition. It is a fundamental need of every human

being. How did we end up expecting that we would emancipate

everyone, when the source of realisation is inherently present in every

human being? It is incredible that all of us have been keeping faith in

such assurances. Now, we must consider whether to have faith in

assurances or to rely on evidence. From my early days, my

tendency has been to trust on the basis of evidence, so I was naturally

encouraged by this approach. My search for evidence led me to

80 reconsider. As a result, I am committed to presenting my findings to

humankind.

Just as all seven billion people on Earth are currently facing a dead

end, you can imagine that I too found myself in a similar situation. I

have also navigated through the clutter of modern education,

sanskar, and rituals prevalent in the world. However, my acceptance

remained neither with modern education nor with traditional

idealistic sanskar. My faith could not stabilise in these. This became

the basis and reason for my pursuit of absolute objectives. Unable to

find faith in either modern education or idealistic tradition, I was

compelled to embark on an independent exploration.

Two significant events have occurred. First, I understood jeevan,

which inherently contains understanding. Second, I found a way of

living with understanding. We operate in four and a half activities on

the basis of beliefs and faith. Faith means believing without knowing.

Trust means believing after knowing. The ten activities of jeevan

become evident when living with trust. I evidence all ten activities,

and so can you. Humans must evidence coexistence. The atoms and

molecules too exist in orderliness while recognising one another. All

the planets, celestial bodies, vegetation, and minerals are in

orderliness, evidencing coexistence.

At the fundamental level, all units are energised within themselves to

evidence coexistence. This existence is a wonderful manifestation of

being energised only. All atomic particles, all atoms, and all molecules

81 have an inherent orientation towards orderliness. This itself is the

main inspiration for humans. In my view, every scholar, scientist and

lay person needs a coexistence mindset. It is only with this mindset

that we can become humane. Anything short of humaneness is not

going to give rise to our splendour.

The forests, hills, minerals, and animals that surround us have

manifested their grandeur through coexistence alone. They thrive

through the way of coexistence. Without coexistence, nothing

would be protected. At the fundamental level, every entity is

protected, regulated, and energised by Omnipotence. While

those working in the form of molecules and biological cells have

specific functions, the grandeur of coexistence is evident even in this.

The coexistence of one cell (pran kosha) with another cell leads to

multicellular forms, resulting in the formation of definite organisms.

The method of formation is inherent in the pran sutra (genetic

material) situated in the cell. This is called rachna vidhi (genetic

code). These pran sutras have continuous search activity in them,

which is evidenced by the multitude of diverse organisms we observe.

This evidence assures us of the presence of search activity in pran

sutras and even in atomic particles.

Imaginativeness and free will are the sources of human search

activity. Additionally, the powers of thought, desire, resolve, and

realisation-evidence in jeevan remain dedicated to search and

exploration. Only through this dedication does the grandeur of all

ten activities of jeevan become evident in human living. The primary

82 objective of these ten activities is attaining realisation and being able

to live based on realisation. The source of realisation-based living is

inherent in jeevan. Humans inherently aspire for wisdom and believe

themselves to be wise, realised, judicious, and contemplative.

Relationships are present all around in existence. Knowing,

believing, recognising, and fulfilling these relationships, and finding

mutual satisfaction as a result, itself would be evidence of

judiciousness.

Humans are free to choose whether or not they want to become wise.

If they choose to become wise then there are always conditions in

existence for becoming wise. All the content is available for becoming

wise. If they choose not to become wise then existence has content

for that as well, but the results of the two choices are different.

Happiness or good is not going to happen in ignorance. I have never

wanted to live while being tied up with something, as a burden on

someone, or while fighting anyone. In the same way, you would also

not want to live while being tied up with something, as a burden on

someone, or while fighting anyone. No one wants to live being

trapped. In this way, every human has a desire within to become wise.

They want to live harmoniously with justice and resolution.

The relationships are all around us, yet due to delusion, we fail to

recognise them. This is the root cause of our troubles. Once we start

to understand and acknowledge these relationships, the inherent

values of jeevan begin to flow naturally. Consequently, relationships

become fulfilling, leading to mutual satisfaction upon evaluation.

83 This is how justice manifests. The conditions and methods of

recognising relationships arise from their intended purposes.

Children recognise 'mother' as the nurturer. The provider of

protection is known as 'father'. The source of knowledge and

guidance is referred to as 'guru', and the source of curiosity and

learning is known as 'disciple'.

The prevailing belief nowadays is that we should strive to live with

the efficiency of machines. But is a human truly a machine? Can

anyone own up and answer this question? I assert that humans are

not machines; rather, they are the creators of all machines ever

devised. A machine can never come close to emulating human

capabilities. In fact, any machine will always fall short in comparison

to humans. Therefore, a machine can never truly understand a

human. Furthermore, all machines are made from insentient nature.

Every machine constructed thus far has been made from

entities of the material order alone. It's noteworthy that not a

single machine has been created from entities of biological

order, still they boast that humans are machines! How far would

this be appropriate for human tradition? How would this satisfy the

intent of comprehensive resolution in humans? While it may be

ingrained in contemporary thought that humans are nothing more

than machines and consumers, the reality is quite different. When

one experiences the bond with their child, they undoubtedly

recognise that they are not merely mechanical entities.

84 I recognised humans with humane consciousness only. Humane

consciousness is the combined form of conscience and sensitivity. If I

am not sensitive, I become like a machine. We humans have not yet

found satisfaction in such mechanistic living. We have been unable to

find satisfaction while working like machines. I challenge any guru

who claims to have found such a path. Even after listening to

geneticists, I remain unconvinced. Similarly, neither materialistic nor

relativistic theories have succeeded in defining the human being. If

human nature could be fully analysed based on these theories, then

they could be accepted. Otherwise, humans should be acknowledged

for what they truly are. This proposal aims to recognise humans as

they truly are.

Before this, idealism presented God as the one responsible for

deliverance. I have seen God; He does not have a factory for

deliverance. In what form did I see God? I saw God as

Omnipresence. I saw God as the absolute energy in which every unit

is energised. I have seen that every unit in Omnipresence is in

coexistence. What more is there to be seen in God? If there is

anything more, you are welcome to explore and reveal it to the world!

You are free to explore. What I have seen and understood has already

been presented before you.

We have failed to achieve completeness through either sensitivity or

machine-like efficiency. Sensory contact becomes the focus in the way

of sensitivity. Thus, one discovers that their sensory capacity and

expectations differ even from those of their own brother. This

85 necessitates dividing humans based on their sensitivity.

Consequently, the path of sensitivity leads humans towards

individualism. Similarly, the pursuit of machine-like efficiency

propels humans towards individualism through consumerism, as we

have already witnessed. The third path, bestowed upon us by our

ancestors, is devotionism and asceticism. There is no end to

individualism here either. Despite all the hard work, tireless efforts,

and best intentions of humans, everything has ended up in failure

due to individualism. Individualism is anti-coexistence and has

become the basis for the fragmentation of humankind.

Where can one live apart from coexistence? The simple solution for

living in coexistence is to know, believe, and recognise coexistence

within humans. If this is recognised, then one becomes capable of

living in orderliness and participating in the universal orderliness,

about which we will study subsequently. Such living includes living

in coexistence with the animal world and the plant world as well. If

we take something from the plant world, then we should have

something to give back as well. If we want to only take and not give

anything, it is selfishness, which ultimately leads to frustration and

suffering. The events unfolding today serve as a testament to this

reality.

To live in coexistence, it is essential to ascertain our coexistence with

the mineral, plant, and animal worlds. Failure to do so renders us

neither scholars, scientists, nor wise. In essence, our knowledge,

science, and wisdom remain incomplete without this fundamental

86 understanding. How will we live without the plants, Earth,

mountains, minerals, and animals? We have to live with all these. All

this matter, treasures, and splendours of nature have to exist along

with us. These need to exist, and we need to coexist with them.

Humans are central to ensuring this coexistence. Humans, being in

delusion, have lived in frustration and suffering. Now, there is a need

to turn the tide. Humans need to awaken and recognise coexistence

with everything. The way of recognising coexistence, I found, is to

see that all these are present in Omnipotence (Space), which is the

first testimony of coexistence. The biological order has emerged, is

influenced, and has a continuity of its splendour from the material

order. The biological order in itself is effective, evident, and

splendorous in the form of orderliness. The animal world is also

evident in the form of inherent orderliness. Humans need to

evidence their inherent orderliness.

How will humans understand their self and inherentness? Self

should also be understood, and inherentness should also be

understood. One understands both self and inherentness from jeevan

vidya. I recognise jeevan in the form of ‘self’, and so can you. We

remain in delusion till we believe the body to be the self. I started

living in orderliness from the moment I recognised jeevan as ‘self’.

You will also be able to live thus. Orderliness is not going to happen

before that. Understanding this is such a natural, co-existentially

complete process, where jeevan is the entity that understands, and

jeevan itself is the entity to be understood.

87 According to idealists, liberation occurs when drishta (the one who

sees), drishya (that which is to be seen), and darshan (the knowledge

from seeing) becomes one. According to them God is the drishta,

God is the drishya and God is the darshan. A great deal has been

written based on these premises. Still, it is not understood - What is

God? Where is God? Why is God? In spite of this, people listen to

such discourses because it feels good. It has been observed that the

gap between feeling good and being good remains unchanged.

Subsequently, some began to describe humans as machines. This

concept too did not succeed, yet they continued to advocate for it.

Just as they couldn't adequately explain God, yet persisted in

discussing it. In this way, we have become stuck, unable to think of

anything beyond this. The way out of this situation is to begin with

the premise that jeevanis eternal and body is a recurring event for

jeevan. The body gets formed in the womb. An atom attains jeevan

status upon development through a natural process in existence.

The body gets formed and deformed repeatedly. Biological cells,

which constitute the body, have a limited lifespan after which they

decompose. The human body, particularly the brain, represents the

pinnacle of evolutionary completeness in the biological order. On

this basis, I assert that humans are capable of conveying the

knowledge of the entire existence to others. The brain's purpose

culminates in this ability. Consequently, the human body, formed

through successive explorations of rachna vidhi (the genetic code) in

pran sutras, is the most advanced formation of biological order. If

88 there is anything left to be discovered, it will be in the future.

Meanwhile, what should we do in our lifetimes? We must evidence

jeevan’s awakening. As we humans embarked on this journey, our

sensitivity could not be concealed, neither by science nor by idealism.

Numerous penances have been suggested to subdue the senses, and

many ascetics have practised them on Earth. However, their penance

did not lead to the definitive understanding that humans have

yearned for—an understanding that could manifest in behaviour and

tradition. It is now up to these ascetics to testify to what they have

discovered. Ordinary people have followed these ascetics in

expectation of miracles and supernatural feats, much like being in a

trance. Let me clarify that existence does not hold miracles or

supernatural phenomena. Existence operates with definite

orderliness, outcomes, accomplishments, and milestones, and these

have continuity—I have observed and understood this. All humans

aspire to reach such a definitive destination, which can only be

achieved through a definitive method. We cannot attain the definitive

destination of humanity without studying humans as a reality within

existence. Neither can we achieve this by disregarding the study of

humans and proclaiming cockroaches as the most evolved species,

nor by destroying Earth with chemical fertilisers and insecticides.

Humans will not reach their destination by treating human intellect

as a commodity or using it for exploitation, which is termed as

“intellectual property right.” The highest institutions and judicial

courts of the world are seeking to accept and legalise intellectual

89 property rights. Jeevan’s powers are inexhaustible—how can these be

classified or treated as commodities? Can anyone provide an answer?

Have these proposals been made with an understanding of jeevan?

To what extent would this be beneficial for humankind? In my

experience, the powers of jeevan do not diminish regardless of how

extensively they are used. This is something that anyone can

experience and verify. The more jeevan’s powers are used, the more

renewed and radiant they become.

The powers of jeevan are boundless and cannot be depleted through

use. Attempting to quantify these powers only leads to frustration.

This illustrates how we succumb to intellectualism, becoming

commodities to be exploited, leading to slavery and the foundation of

exploitation. In my opinion, it is fundamentally against humanity

and coexistence to exploit human intellect, to use it as a source of

conflict, or to claim ownership over it. To suggest that a just society

can be built upon the trade of human intellect is a falsehood that

warrants serious consideration. I firmly believe that the notion of

limited human intellect is a blatant lie. Every individual possesses an

inexhaustible intellectual capacity that transcends the confines of

books. I, myself, am greater than all the books I have written, just as

every human is greater than all the books combined. Until we accept

this truth, I don’t think we can do anything wisely.

After all this discussion, perhaps everyone can think through and

accept that which is right. We must become wise; that is the only final

conclusion that emerges. There are no major difficulties in becoming

90 wise. The difficulties are only while we experiment in ignorance.

Earth is an indivisible whole, yet humans create divisions and

perceive it as separate nations. Moreover, we deploy armies along

these divisions and engage in conflict repeatedly. Fragmenting the

Earth is not feasible, and no one would survive such fragmentation.

Is there any merit in believing that the Earth is divided? This prompts

us to reflect on the depth of deception we have succumbed to.

Consider another example: our classification of humans based on

skin colour and race, treating them as if they were animals. What sort

of intelligence is this? The true measure of humans lies in their

understanding, not in their skin colour or race. History is replete

with instances such as revolts against slavery and feudalism.

Feudalism has given way to democracy, yet we have not succeeded in

establishing systems based on socialistic and humanistic principles,

despite believing that we have. The lie lies in our belief that we have

achieved, when in reality, all that we have achieved is some amenities

of comfort. Wars, conflicts, and exploitation still persist. The sources

of deception lie in the concept of the nation, rooted in the false belief

in Earth's fragmentation, and in the idea of a Constitution based on

power-centric rule. They say Nation and Constitution are above

everything. The essence of this Constitution is - power-centric rule.

What is a power-centric rule? It is the attempt to stop one mistake

by committing another, to stop one crime by perpetrating

another, and to stop one war by inciting another. Some

constitutions include provisions for providing basic facilities to all.

91 The underlying rationale here is that if everyone possesses wealth,

they can fend for themselves. 'We must struggle to survive,' they

proclaim. According to them, our identity is defined solely by our

capacity to endure hardship. But do these proclamations hold any

truth? They serve as the foundation of numerous falsehoods. Our

concepts of family, education, business, and more are built upon

these falsehoods. Consequently, we find ourselves submerged

beneath layers of deceit. While some strive to break free, the majority

remain ensnared. We desire to change education to overcome this

predicament.

We are now ready to evidence the ten activities of jeevan. Every

human has a tacit acceptance of jeevan’s existence, since every human

claims to be alive on their own. Still, we don’t understand what

jeevanis? What is the purpose of jeevan? Who studies jeevan? I have

understood the ten activities of jeevan, practised these in living, and

these have become evident in me. Let’s first become familiar with the

names of ten activities of jeevan.

1.​Atma: - atma is a part of jeevanwhich attains realisation in

coexistence. I have seen it as the nucleus. It remains active as

the nucleus of a constitutionally complete atom. All other

activities of jeevantake place in its first, second, third and

fourth orbits. There are only two activities in the nucleus of

jeevanatom - realisation (anubhav) and authenticity

(pramanikta) - which have been evidenced in me.

92

2.​Buddhi: - I have seen two activities: enlightenment (bodh) of

realisation-evidence and resolve (sankalp) happening in the

first orbit of jeevan. The resolve activity is for evidencing the

realisation-evidence, which is called resoluteness (ritambhara).

3.​Chitta: - The second orbit has two activities: contemplation

(chintan) and visualisation (chitran).

4.​Vritti: - The third orbit has two activities: deliberation (tulan)

and analysis (vishleshan).

5.​Mun: - The fourth orbit has two activities: taste (asvadan)

and selection (chayan). These are all the ten activities of

jeevan.

Until now, humans have only manifested four and a half activities of

jeevan, deliberating solely with the perspectives of pleasure, health,

and profit. They have operated based on sensitivity, which originates

from the body's senses. However, it is jeevan itself that animates these

senses. The root of delusion lies in identifying jeevan with the body.

Once jeevan identifies with the body, it is bound to function

according to bodily needs. This adherence to 'belief'—rather than

'knowledge'—forms the basis of delusion.

What should be there instead? Jeevan should be recognised as jeevan,

and the body as the body. Evaluating jeevan and the body naturally

occurs based on their respective purposes. When this occurs, living

with humane consciousness and orderliness ensues. Without this

assessment, disorder in human life is inevitable. Orderliness in

93 human existence necessitates evaluating jeevan based on its purpose

and the body based on its utility. The body serves as a vessel for

jeevan's awakening in human tradition.

Humans have not created the human body; upon birth, when a child

is already alive due to jeevan's presence, we mistakenly identify the

body as jeevan itself. Over time, the child adopts this misconception,

perpetuating the cycle. To break free from this cycle, guardians and

parents must attain wisdom.

A child’s body forms in the womb and is driven by a jeevan. This

jeevan, already present in nature, begins to animate the body from

the fourth or fifth month of pregnancy. Thus, jeevan and body unite

within the womb. It's essential to understand that jeevan is distinct

from the body. This distinction becomes apparent when we consider

that no part of the body anticipates or expects justice, dharma, or

truth. However, we expect and anticipate justice, dharma, and truth

from every human being. These expectations being fulfilled is the

manifestation of the ten activities of jeevan.

Jeevanhas to be there with the body for it to be alive. ‘Jeevan’ starts

evidencing the two activities of mun that are taste (asvadan) and

selection (chayan) from the infant stage itself. Subsequently, analysis

(vishleshan) takes place in vritti, but deliberation (tulan) happens

based on pleasure, health and profit only. One of the activities of

chitta – visualisation (chitran) – we do anyway. Humans have

visualised and accomplished all the objects of their common and

94 special aspirations because of visualisation activity. Even after

accomplishing these, we could not achieve orderliness.

Idealism presented lofty ideals in various forms, while materialism

and its three obsessions (for sex, consumption, and profit) fostered a

culture of comfort and accumulation through education and

training programmes. However, despite these efforts, widespread

comfort and accumulation remained elusive. We deluded ourselves

into believing that these achievements were the result of our

excellence and humanity, a rightful reward for our struggle and

exploitation. It’s both laughable and pitiful to assume that through

these, we have fulfilled all human needs or comprehensively

understood human nature.

Consider the biological sciences, which focus solely on the

body's structure and functions yet claim to impart the study of

the human being. Can we truly understand a human being by

dissecting the body, counting muscles and bones? Can we grasp the

essence of a human being by examining eyes, ears, and other bodily

organs? Such practices perpetuate a cycle of deception within human

tradition. We boast of having understood human beings and

mastering existence, yet in reality, we are burdened by our own lies.

Now, we face two options: either free ourselves from this burden or

perish beneath its weight. We are taught that destiny corrects its

course by itself, and after humans have done all the excesses they can,

conditions may arise where humans cannot even survive on Earth.

95 There's already a lot of noise about the environment, with estimates

on who will survive and who will perish. Some countries hope to

safeguard their nation, while some religions seek salvation for their

followers. They find solace in the belief of a saviour, referred to as

God, Paramatma, deity, avatar, or messiah. Such narratives often

imply that only followers of a certain faith will be saved, while others

are doomed. But where does this lead us? What does such thinking

achieve?

In my view, both State and Religion are at a loss when it comes to

education. Religious institutions lack a universal foundation for

dharma, devoid of education and evidence. So, where does dharma

stand?

Similarly, in all the seats of State, there is no concept of State which

we could call universal. They proclaim the need to work towards

saving the State. But how will they achieve that? Through struggle,

they say. Struggle is all about revolt, rebellion, exploitation, and war.

Who prepares these four – nature or humans? Upon examination, it

becomes clear that humans, driven by delusion, are the ones who

perpetrate all this.

The two most dominant seats of power—Religion and State—wield

all the resources and authority. Yet, they fail to provide solutions for

the human condition. It’s futile to seek answers from the

profit-driven seat of commerce, which is inherently exploitative.

Similarly, when questioned, the seat of education falls short in

96 offering clear guidance or purpose. So, what is the common person to

do? None of these institutions offer direction. The courageous path

forward lies in discovering or forging a new way. This path embodies

understanding, honesty, responsibility, and participation. The path

of conflict leads nowhere; humans cannot fulfil their needs through

conflict, yet it remains ingrained in our tradition. Isn't this also a

significant delusion? Now, the only sensible course of action is that

we become wise. Understanding is verified within oneself through

acceptance and the study of developed consciousness. You cannot

attain understanding by examining me; you will become wise only

when you examine yourself. For thirty years of my life, I kept

examining others fruitlessly, finding no trace of understanding. I

found understanding only when I examined myself after my sadhana

of twenty-five years. I aim to share the fruits of this journey with

humanity in a format conducive to study. This is an endeavour in this

course.

By now, it must have become indicated to you that coexistence itself

is the ultimate truth. Living in coexistence is our ultimate dharma - if

this becomes clear, then all the understanding required for it is within

your grasp. It’s very simple. According to me, living a lie is more

difficult than living truthfully. Truthful living is simpler, I have seen

it by living. Living was so difficult when I was surrounded with

questions. When I found the resolution, I became free from all

questions, and life became simple. If this resonates with you as well, it

will only strengthen my conviction. Those who are with me have

97 experienced it; if you desire the same, you too can verify it. The

verification of this proposal begins from deliberation whether our

behaviour is according to justice. Have we understood relationships

and are we able to fulfil them? Are we able to evaluate the inherent

values in relationships? Are we able to reach the point of mutual

satisfaction or not? These are all aspects of verification. As we embark

on this journey of verification, we realise that there is no certainty in

the perspectives of pleasure, health, and profit. That which I find

pleasant, may not be pleasant to you. That which I feel is healthy,

may not feel healthy to you. The level of profit that satisfies you may

not suffice for me. All humans are ensnared in this trap. Therefore,

equality cannot be based on the perspectives of pleasure, health, and

profit.

To break free from this trap, we need to replace the three perspectives

of deliberation (pleasure, health, and profit) with three alternative

perspectives: justice, dharma, and truth. As we begin deliberating

from the perspective of justice, it is called contemplation. Justice is

comprehended only upon recognising relationships within the

framework of orderliness. As relationships are recognised, fulfilment

of values commences, culminating in evaluation and mutual

satisfaction. This is what justice entails—satisfying both sides in a

balanced manner. It cannot be deemed just if both sides are not

content. Someone once asked me what should be done with those

who commit crimes or wrongs. They do so because we fail to guide

them towards wisdom. Why do you focus on criminals and not on

98 those who are righteous? For instance, I don’t commit any crimes or

wrongs. Many others like me abstain from criminal acts, and we

don’t have any problems with them. How can you ignore or deny this

reality? It serves as evidence for you to consider. Now the crucial

question arises: do you have a need for this understanding or not?

From my perspective, you need this understanding above all else. All

humans are eagerly awaiting this understanding alone. The only

difference between you and me is that I took a step forward out of my

anguish, attained this understanding, and have become capable of

attesting to it. You, too, will bear witness in the same manner once

you grasp the immense happiness and satisfaction that comes from

living in accordance with justice. It is not solely for my testimony;

you can also testify. All humans will become capable of testifying in

the same way once they understand.

The understanding will be disseminated through educational

institutions. An educational institution is a collective expression of all

parents and guardians. Education is the activity of evidencing the

understanding upon enlightenment. Without understanding,

enlightenment of evidence – there is no education. The

responsibility for imparting understanding lies with educational

institutions and all parents and guardians. Every family is intricately

linked with education. Hence, contemplating the unification,

privatization, or nationalization of educational institutions has not

proven beneficial in the past, nor will it be in the future. The

parents and guardians should be directly recognised as

99 educational institutions. This approach alone will prove beneficial

for humankind, as it aligns with the principles of understanding.

We must become proficient at dispensing justice. The capacity of

dispensing justice will need to become evident in us. Only when we

acquire these two qualities can we truly dispense justice, and only

then can we claim to have understood. Without understanding, how

can we do justice? When even the judges in the highest courts lack

understanding of justice, what hope is there for ordinary people?

Justice is the minimum requirement for human living. The evidence

of justice is in the form of humane conduct. Anything short of

humane conduct has no justice at all. More than that is not even

needed.

Jeevanhas six activities functioning with contemplation (chintan).

We have done a great deal of analysis (vishleshan) for pleasure, health

and profit. We have been able to produce a lot of things related to our

common and special aspirations. Apart from these, we have also

produced things such as bombs, missiles, and warships which are not

useful for humans. These things are meaningless and are causes of

destruction. It can be understood by logic and also by seeing the

events in the history.

Humans engage with realities existentially, logically and

behaviourally. We want to become happy existentially. As we become

happy existentially, we evidence this existential realisation in our

behaviour only through logic. Logic is the basis with which we do

100 everything like reading, writing, and talking. Meaningful logic

touches existentiality, which is the magnificence of communication.

My communication is meaningful if existentiality becomes indicated

through it to another person. Meaningfulness of behaviour is in

instilling the understanding in other that the human purpose is

resolution, prosperity, fearlessness and coexistence. This is how

realisation in behavioural knowledge takes place. This is also the way

existential knowledge takes place in another person. Therefore, logic

is needed both for existential knowledge and behavioural knowledge.

The first accomplishment of this knowledge is we having the basis of

our own evaluation and evaluation of our family members. The

evaluation will be on the basis of values, relationships, and evidence

of mutual satisfaction. We can evidence being judicious in our

behaviour. It is only then that a human becomes humane.

Thereafter, one becomes autonomous based on understanding and

attains the following six merits.

1. Self-confidence

1. Respect for Excellence

1. Balance in Talent

1. Balance in Personality

1. Social in Behaviour

1. Self-reliant in Vocation

101 It is upon attaining these six merits that I felt to have attained

autonomy. Hence, I became capable of evidencing my understanding

and prosperity in the family. I am presenting it before you with this

truthfulness. Every person must be wanting to become civilised,

while the minimum qualification for civility is justice. Justice, as I see

it, is - relationship, values, evaluation and mutual satisfaction. After

this, I also understood that every human seeks justice from the

moment of their birth. They naturally want to work and behave

correctly. They naturally speak the truth. On this basis, what should

be the content of education? Every human child should be

enlightened, they should get practice to do correct work and

behaviour, and the capability of delivering justice should be instilled

in them. All of these three aspects need to be there in an educational

institution, which will pave the way for humane tradition on its own.

Humane tradition will not happen without this.

Humane tradition has to start with justice. The core of justice is in

understanding that our relationship with natural surroundings is

timeless and our relationship with other humans is continuous.

When someone makes a mistake then where do they go for guidance?

First someone from their family, who lives with justice, gives

guidance. If not from family then someone in the village gives

guidance. If there is nobody to guide in the village also, then they will

try looking for someone in their country or the whole Earth. It is a

natural human tendency. Every human has a natural tendency for

reforming themselves somewhere or the other.

102 It has become evident that the world wants a change, but what

change they want was not clear so far. This proposal addresses it.

Education alone will result in dissemination of this proposal. There

should be provision for humane education in the educational

institutions.

We will have to impart the understanding for every person to become

evidence of living with justice. We will have to impart study of

sentience along with science for this. Unless we understand sentience,

we cannot grasp the understanding of existence, and if we don’t

understand existence then how will we understand its orderliness.

The one who understands existence is jeevan(unit of sentience).

Therefore, the study of jeevanhas to be incorporated in education.

Psychology needs to incorporate the sanskaraspect (understanding)

i.e. the aspect of humane consciousness. Humane consciousness is

the grandeur of both conscience and sensitivity. Philosophy should

be taught with a realised human as its evidence. On doing so, the way

of humaneness will prevail - and not materialism or spiritualism.

Therefore, humans can become wise, and existence is always available

for understanding.

My realisation about evidence is that it lies in enabling others to

understand, learn, and do, as I have understood, learnt, and done.

Evidence is necessary in all these three aspects, and there isn’t a fourth

aspect to it. It is acceptable if our learning and doing falls short, but

understanding must be complete. So far, we have accomplished

much in learning and doing, but we are nowhere in terms of

103 understanding. At present, learning and doing are considered to be

the most valuable, but this has brought us neither resolution nor

relief, and we continue getting stuck somewhere or the other.

Therefore, the need has arisen for humans to study the entire

existence and gain self-confidence. It becomes natural for humans to

demonstrate understanding after study and practice. Humans must

verify their understanding through their own study and practice.

The study of humans was left behind in the pursuit of idealism and

materialism. In Idealism the deities and God are considered to be

above all, and humans got left behind. They sacrificed study of

humans in an attempt to understand the deities and God.

Materialism too left humans aside, brought machines to the fore by

experimentation method, and made machines the basis of evidence.

While scriptures, books and literature became the evidence in

idealism, the machine became the evidence in materialism. In this

way, humans got under-valued, and being trapped in delusion they

ended up only furthering that delusion. Thus, being trapped in

delusion, led to humans suffering, becoming frustrated, and harassed.

Now how will the deliverance of humans come about? All seats of

power have been giving such assurances, but there is no evidence of

deliverance. How long can it go on like this?

The alternative proposed here is - understanding is the fundamental

source of human deliverance. The highest authority for fostering this

understanding lies within the education system. Education should

encompass the study of consciousness alongside science. How can we

104 study coexistence without exploring consciousness? These two

critical aspects have remained untouched in educational institutions,

their content, and pedagogy. Secondly, in psychology, humane

consciousness is studied, understood and evidenced. Therefore, the

aspect of sanskar should be integrated into psychological studies.

Thirdly, philosophical studies must be grounded in evidence.

Our belief until now has been that one who can repeat what they

have read, has become ‘learned’. However, this does not truly make

one learned. True wisdom embodies understanding, with knowledge

being natural and aligned with the realities of existence. Without

understanding coexistence, jeevan, and humane conduct, one cannot

be genuinely learned.

As these aspects are understood, a coherent thought process

develops, leading to planning and the creation of structured

programs, ultimately resulting in verifiable outcomes. Without

understanding, how can we develop a meaningful thought process?

In the absence of understanding, one prevalent way of thinking is the

pursuit of comfort and accumulation. The other is idealism, which

focuses on renunciation, non-accumulation, detachment, and

devotion. Millions have devoted themselves to idealism,

demonstrating their courage, patience, and dedication. Yet, neither of

these ideologies has led to the emergence of an indivisible society.

Humans have worked tirelessly but without a clear, universal human

goal or direction. My endeavour was solely to find answers to my

105 questions. I had no aspirations of attaining heaven, wealth, or

material accumulation. My only resolve was that if I had a doubt, I

would inevitably find the answer.

I will now explain the meaning of ‘yog’ and ‘sanyog’. The meaning of

yog is coming together. For example, if we are going somewhere and

we come across a rock, or another person – that’s called yog. Sanyog

means to come together for completeness. Completeness means

humans living in orderliness. The ultimate completeness means

humans becoming authentic. Humans inherently want to live in

orderliness and become authentic, but when that want is not

fulfilled, they helplessly get moulded according to tradition. Yog and

sanyog are always there in existence. There have been many efforts in

history for completeness (their becoming successful is another

matter). Humans have made many sacrifices for achieving

completeness. Sacrifices eventually lead to something.

In the process of breaking a boulder, the success becomes visible with

the final strike, but it is the cumulative effect of all preceding strikes

that makes the final strike successful. The success I achieved is also

due to the contribution of all prior efforts. Therefore, I acknowledge

that this event is a result of the entire humankind’s collective

contribution. A significant benefit of this understanding is that it

prevented me from becoming arrogant about my success.

Additionally, very few people who exhibit arrogance have approached

me. Even those who initially displayed arrogance experienced a

reduction in their egotism after a few interactions.

106 Everyone who met me did so with civility, simplicity, and naturalness.

However, this doesn’t mean that everyone who met me accepted my

ideas. Many people did not, and I respect their stance as well. It is not

their fault; they are burdened by tradition. Consequently, I remain

content whether someone accepts my ideas or not. Each human

being carries the seed of righteousness within them, and the sanyog

must occur for this seed to flourish. When and how this will happen,

we cannot predict. Every human desires good to prevail. I aim to

bring the possibilities of its realisation within reach.

Sanyog occurs when humans come together for the sake of
