unacceptable. Foolishness, conflict, revolt, rebellion and fighting are

unacceptable to me. Materialism asserts that nothing can happen

without revolt and rebellion. In contrast, Resolution Centred

Materialism posits that everything in existence has inherent strength.

This inherent strength manifests as use, right-use, and

purposeful-use, which are the natural essences of an awakened life.

The main issue is whether science can be aligned with wisdom.

Wisdom means recognition of the purpose. Purpose should align

with science, and science should align with wisdom. Science aligned

with wisdom means humans becoming capable of analysing

purposes. Until science can analyse purposes, its logic is

incomplete.

So far, proponents of science have claimed to provide logical

materialism. If that is true, the first logical question is: what am I?

Who am I? Why am I? How do our peace, unrest, happiness, and

unhappiness arise? Why do we suffer? Why do we feel happy? Science

does not provide answers to these questions. We cannot reach the

truth by starting with a lie. There is resolution, destiny, and the

course of destiny in existence. The course of destiny means

158 movements towards resolution, which I have tried to explain in

Resolution Centred Materialism.

Behaviour Centred Public Discourse is also written on the same

basis. Humans want to become happy, and resolution = happiness,

problem = unhappiness. One must have resolution. How will

resolution happen? It will happen through behaviour. How will that

happen? We will become resolved through relationship, values,

evaluation and mutual satisfaction. We remain afflicted with

problems as long as we don't recognise relationships and till we don’t

fulfil values according to relationships. Resolution happens when

relationships, values, evaluation, and mutual satisfaction come

together. This coming together transforms four problems into one

resolution. Humans have become buried under problems. Anywhere

you see there are only problems and humans are nowhere to be seen.

The result is endless social, political, cultural and economic problems

that have eclipsed humans. Every human life ends struggling with

problems generation after generation. Its alternative, Behaviour

Centred Public Discourse postulates that humans become resolved

through behaviour. Behaviour happens in our relationship with

humans and in our relationship with the natural surroundings. All

our behaviour with natural surroundings has to be according to law,

regulation and balance for us to find resolution, otherwise we

become afflicted from problems there - which is our present

condition. We engaged in industrial activity without right

understanding, tore Earth’s guts apart, and as a result we are

159 suffering. These problems have raised a question mark on human

survival on this planet. In my view, every human can become

resolved, irrespective of who they are and what they do. That’s what

is postulated in Behaviour Centred Public Discourse. Its essence is -

relationships, values, evaluation and mutual satisfaction. This itself

leads to our attaining all round resolution. Economic resolution

comes from understanding the cyclicality of nature. A cultured way

of living is achieved through Psychology of Humane Consciousness.

Humans are units of the knowledge order; therefore, they can

evidence themselves only through cognitive ability. It is about

recognising relationships, having trust in the present, living in

orderliness and evidencing coexistence. In this way, Behaviour

centred Public Discourse has been postulated for comprehensive

resolution.

Question: Freud has put forth a postulation which claims that

all desires of humans have a single origin, and that is sex.

People worldwide have accepted this ideology in a declared or

undeclared way. However, we see that it has not resulted in a

clear and resolving contemplation about humans. You have

talked about “Psychology of Humane Consciousness.” How

will this replace Freudian psychology? How will humans

achieve peace and happiness by understanding it, and how will

humankind find the right direction?

Answer: Every human is a combined form of jeevan and body, as has

been explained. Jeevan is essentially a constitutionally complete atom.

160 An insentient atom itself undergoes transcendence and becomes

sentient (jeevan). It is then that nature achieves the grandeur of its

sentient form. A constitutionally complete atom is free from

molecular and gravitational bonds, and this itself is its grandeur. It

becomes capable of driving a body with an evolved brain through

coexistence. Both body and jeevan are definite accomplishments in

the course of destiny in existence. Humans and animals are combined

forms of jeevan and body. This has been thoroughly observed and

can be studied. This study focuses on understanding the statuses of

being alive, not being alive, being with jeevan, and being without

jeevan. The evidence of being with jeevan is understood from sensory

activity. When jeevan cannot express itself through the body or when

sensory activities cease, we declare that the person is no more. Death

means jeevan has left the body.

Death is proclaimed from the instant that jeevanseparates from the

body. We don’t call that body to be human. Human is recognised

while jeevanis driving the body. Every human is a thinking entity.

Animals don’t have any scope for imaginative thinking. The

conscious activity in animals is only in the form of species

conformity. Even if humans want to live like animals, the reach of

their imaginativeness and free will goes far beyond that limit. As

human thought was never contained within the purview of the body,

it was natural for us to spread out far and wide. We (Jeevan) could

not be limited by the body due to this reason. We could not become

satisfied and resolved by thinking within bodily limits for the same

161 reason. Its testimony is that we neither became social nor the

indivisible society materialised. We didn’t achieve universal

orderliness. The orderliness of dogs is universal, orderliness of horses

is universal, and orderliness of every animal is universal. Why are

humans so unfortunate that their orderliness cannot be universal?

Each entity in existence - donkey, horse, dog, grass, stone, iron, gems -

has its use, and they are complementary to one another. How is it

possible to be a human and not be complementary?

Thinking is intrinsic to us. We humans cannot remain silent.

Silencing thoughts is not in our hands. Being silent is anti-nature,

anti-destiny, anti-progress, and anti-awakening. In this way, humans

become antagonistic in these four ways by pursuing silence.

Antagonism naturally gives rise to problems, which is what

happened.

Many people have pursued the state of samadhi in our country.

When it came to giving evidence of their having achieved the state of

samadhi, some have given it as well, albeit in a roundabout way.

However, no one could clearly declare that, “I have achieved the state

of samadhi. The result of it is precisely this, and I am its evidence.”

Then came the divine incarnations. All the documents of divine

incarnations in human form are the ultimate flights of human

imagination. This was done only for the good, but it didn’t result in

the good of all. This means, it didn’t result in evidence of resolution,

prosperity, fearlessness, and coexistence. Indivisible society and

universal orderliness could not be evidenced. Every human didn’t

162 become capable of testifying of having become wise. Everyone didn’t

achieve happiness, peace, contentment, and bliss. It is from this

standpoint that I am talking about the failure of these efforts. Its

opposite, materialism talked of accumulation and comfort – which

also didn’t work, and that too has come to the brink of failure.

Success comes only from humane consciousness.

Where does humane consciousness reside? It resides in jeevan, not in

the body. Therefore, Freud, the person you mentioned, has nothing

to do with jeevan. If sexual lust is all that jeevan desires, then this is

already present in animals like dogs and cats. So, what was the need

for the emergence of humans in the course of destiny? If we pose this

question, the only logical conclusion is that human existence has no

purpose. How are humans different from animals then? The goal of

humans is to become happy. To achieve happiness, they need

resolution. No person can evidence prosperity without resolution.

Prosperity without resolution is not possible. Therefore, we need to

think about this. Upon thinking, I understood that humane

consciousness comprises conscience and sensitivity. Conscience has

two aspects: (1) knowing, and (2) believing. Sensitivity also has two

aspects: (1) recognising, and (2) fulfilling. All efforts and propensities

of sensorial living are based on bodily senses. Therefore, all decisions

based on sensitivity will have temporary validity; they will not have

continuity. For example, eating feels good, but one can't keep eating

all the time. Sleeping feels good, but one can't keep sleeping all the

time. Likewise, there is no sensory activity that we could maintain

163 forever in the same way; it needs to change repeatedly. It is not

possible for humans to remain indulged in any sensory activity

without change. Why do we have this complication? This is meant to

orient humans towards humane consciousness. The transient nature

of sensitivity is such a wonderful provision in humans, serving as an

alarm, an inspiration, and a direction for their awakening. This

applies to both you and me. When this awakening arises in you, and

when you will testify to it - that is for you to think about.

Understanding this is your responsibility. I have accomplished all

this, so it is natural for me to feel thrilled. It is so systematic! With a

bit of thoughtfulness, anyone can grasp this. On that basis it became

clear that the sensitivity is transient, while what we want is the

continuity of happiness. We get a glimpse of happiness but there is

no realisation of happiness through sensitivity. Our thirst is for

happiness, which cannot be quenched without realisation.

Realisation is continuous; it does not break apart. On this basis, it

was needed for the continuity of happiness. The transience of

sensations is natural and part of the inherent order. Based on this, we

could evaluate its true value.

After this, I found the meaning of conscience, which is when all

activities of jeevanbecome infused with realisation. This itself is

humane consciousness or awakened consciousness. I have myself

realised it. I impart its study to you. It can only be achieved through

dedicated study. Reading and reciting this repeatedly can aid in

understanding.

164 Understanding jeevan establishes the foundation of humane

consciousness. When humane conduct is understood, it forms the

basis of humane tradition. Without understanding humane

behaviour and humane conduct, humane tradition is not going to

happen. Humane conduct is universally consistent across all times

and places. It combines values, character, and ethics. Character

entails rightfully owned wealth, marital faithfulness, and kindness in

actions and behaviour. Ethics involve the right-use and protection of

body, mind, and wealth. Values are about evaluation and achieving

mutual satisfaction in relationships. The goal of jeevan is

happiness, and the human goal is resolution, prosperity,

fearlessness, and coexistence. Ethics are essential for achieving

these goals and give them purpose. This applies equally to values and

character. We experience unhappiness when there is lack of character,

unethical behaviour, and disregard for values. Therefore, living with

values, character, and ethics is the essence of humane conduct and

intrinsic human nature. To live in this manner, one needs knowledge

of existence, jeevan, and humane conduct.

What is knowledge? Knowing and believing constitute knowledge. It

is only after knowing and believing that one seeks the point of

satisfaction. If we neither know nor believe, why and where would

we search for the point of satisfaction? For instance, we know and

believe in Delhi, which allows us to make plans to visit Delhi. If we

neither know nor believe in Delhi, how could we make such plans?

Similarly, we believed in the existence of the Moon, and we have

165 reached there. We undertake many efforts to reach the point of

satisfaction that comes from knowing and believing. The main

proposition here is that coexistence is understood from

understanding existence, thereupon humane conduct emanates.

Psychology of Humane Consciousness explains all these.

Additionally, I have seen 122 conducts in jeevan. How many of these

122 conducts happen in mun, how many in vritti, how many in

chitta, how many in buddhi, and how many happen in atma - I have

tried to explain it. What is its purpose? The purpose is that as one

listens and gradually understands, they seek the point of satisfaction,

achieved through realisation. This process then enables one to impart

enlightenment to others. Our understanding is evidenced by our

ability to enlighten others. Teaching others demonstrates our

comprehension. Our health is evidenced by our ability to help others

become healthy. Our wealth is evidenced by our ability to help others

become wealthy. This is a simple way of becoming social.

Thus far, humans have only lived within the purview of sensitivity;

hence the issues of accumulation, comfort, revolt-rebellion and

exploitation have kept coming up. Thus, the essence of Psychology of

Humane Consciousness is understanding jeevan’s activities. When

we believe for knowing, then we start living based on knowing, and as

we go about recognising and fulfilling - we become just, regulated,

balanced and happy. This sums up the purpose of “Psychology of

Humane Consciousness”.

166 Question: There are thousands of medical practices on Earth,

and a lot of human effort and money have gone into these. In

spite of this, the health of the human race is still poor. Despite

massive investments and the development of advanced

instruments, the number of diseases is only increasing. New

diseases are emerging constantly. The old techniques do not

achieve the results they claim, and modern techniques also do

not deliver on their promises. In light of this, how do you

recognise health and restraint according to Jeevan Vidya?

Answer: - What you have described is a concern for almost everyone.

All these efforts are aimed at specialisation. However, specialisation is

like a monster, it can be as destructive as a demon. The belief that "we

are specialists, therefore whatever we say is right" has resulted in

numerous offences, especially against those who are ill. When

patients try to explain their ailments, doctors often prefer to rely on

machines rather than listen to them. Machines cannot understand

human suffering. Only a human can truly listen to and comprehend

another human’s pain. Therefore, accurate diagnosis cannot be

achieved solely through the use of instruments.

In the past, the attempts by some people to diagnose ailments

through Ayurveda, Unani, and other methods based on the

knowledge of the pulse were commendable. They tried to identify

illnesses by observing the rate, pressure, flow, strain, and tension of

the pulse, which was praiseworthy. However, over time, doctors

167 found pulse diagnosis challenging and shifted towards the ease of

instrumental diagnosis.

Now, everyone wants to use instruments to diagnose and understand

disease. Decisions based on instruments fail to satisfy the patient, and

the doctor remains distant from recognising the root cause of the

disease. When it comes to drug discovery, research, and

advancements in medical science, it often misses the point. What

needs to be observed is the holistic suitability or adversity of these

treatments for patients, but this is not always the case. All specialists

have become stuck in the pursuit of comfort and accumulation. A

specialist in a big city prescribes the same medicine and treatment as a

small-town doctor but charges a hundred times as much. Patients,

too, think that a doctor who charges more is better! Do you see this

madness? Thirdly, they have never tried to think holistically in

medical science, meaning they’ve never thought of being true

doctors, they have never even tried.

Holistic medical science means to first recognise the state of good

health. Thereafter we assess the state of ailment, which is done by

reading the pulse of the patient, then upon matching it with the

patient’s symptoms – the disease is diagnosed, and a treatment is

given. If the treatment is successful, our understanding will be

considered right, otherwise, it is considered wrong and further

research is needed. This is in contrast with what is prevalent today,

where the doctors say that they are right irrespective of the success or

failure of their treatment. This lack of accountability is dangerous.

168 So, holistic medical science is coming together of – (1) diagnosis of

disease, (2) assessment of the state of ailment, (3) identification of

medicines, (4) identification of potency and combination of

medicines, (5) identification of how the medicine is to be

administered, (6) identification of the patient’s state of mind, (7)

identification of diet regimen, (8) identification of the restraint that

the patient needs to follow, (9) then identification of the way

treatment is to be given. Any disease can be treated fully with yoga

and medicine. The other two aspects in Ayurveda – gem therapy and

mantra therapy have limited use. Gem therapy only talks of rays and

radiations. Mantra therapy primarily affects the mind. Medicine is

the most potent way of treating diseases as it dissolves in bodily

fluids.

The body has an inherent orderliness and the knowledge of healing it

from diseases is intrinsic to it. Doctors often force treatments upon

the body rather than assisting it in its natural healing process. What

should a doctor do? They should support the body's inherent order

by providing suitable substances that strengthen the body’s

condition. This is the true skill, wisdom, and science of a physician.

With such an approach, we can overcome diseases. Therefore, we

should move away from specialised medicine and make it universally

accessible.

Health pertains to the body, while restraint pertains to the mind.

Restraint is based on law, justice, regulation, and balance. Mentality

that operates in a balanced and just manner is known as restraint.

169 What is the remedy for this? Understanding is the remedy. Imbalance

and mental disorders arise from lack of understanding, while balance

comes from understanding. Understanding encompasses the entire

orderliness and balance.

May there be universal well-being!
